The Enterprise SC is a pre-sales role, and as such works closely with Benchling sales leadership, account executives, professional services, and product leaders to ensure the best solutions are presented. Enterprise SCs work with senior scientific and IT leaders from prospects and customers, to establish credibility and confidence from the first meeting, and to create solutions based on cutting-edge technologies.
The Enterprise SC must be comfortable with Life Sciences R&D processes and scientific concepts, have experience with enterprise SaaS solutions, and be adept at working with internal and external leaders and stakeholders. About the role:
ProcessOS is a new kind of Camunda product: business processes described in natural language, generated as executable BPMN workflows, and improved autonomously from production data. We’re hiring the first cohort of Forward Deployed Engineers to bring it into production at enterprise customers. You’ll own the deployment journey from first process file to a working, improving system, and hand off a functioning capability to the customer’s team. The code you write and the patterns you discover feed directly back into how ProcessOS is built. This is a rare opportunity to shape a product, a function, and a field practice from day one.
You’ll work end‑to‑end across Java services and React interfaces, collaborating closely with a talented global team to measure, improve, and scale performance and fault tolerance in real-world distributed systems.
What You’ll Be Doing:
• Deploy and prove. Own the journey from first process file to production workflow. At 90 days: at least one workflow running, the improvement loop active, and measurable fitness gains the customer can see. At 12 months: 3–5 customers with viable deployments.
• Drive organizational adoption. Work across technical and business stakeholders to build understanding and trust, turning early deployments into lasting customer capability.
• Work at depth technically. Configure and run Camunda clusters locally and in cloud environments. Debug integration failures. Build custom agents where platform defaults don’t fit. Write connector logic that gets legacy enterprise systems talking to ProcessOS.
• Build the playbook. There is no deployment template yet. Document what good looks like as you discover it, and make the next implementation faster.
• Feed the product. Custom agents you write get contributed back. Integration patterns get codified. Production bugs you find, you often fix. Your field work is a direct input to ProcessOS.
• Hand off deliberately. Leave customers with a team that can operate independently, is trained on the platform, and acts on improvement results without you.
What You Will Bring to the Role
Must Haves:
• Enterprise production experience: you’ve shipped something inside a large organization and stayed to see it operate. You know why governance and resilience matter at scale.
• Technical depth: You can debug an integration failure, write a custom agent against a legacy API, stand up a Camunda cluster from scratch, and explain generated BPMN to both engineers and business leads.
• Stakeholder communication: you work effectively across engineering, architecture, and business leadership and adapt how you communicate without losing precision.
• Practical AI experience: you’ve used AI to solve real problems in production – not just experimented. You understand context management, prompt engineering, agent testing, and integration tradeoffs.
• Comfort with ambiguity: you make sound judgment calls without a playbook and document what you learn.
• Occasional travel may be required
Nice to Haves:
• Experience in a customer-facing engineering or professional services role.
• Familiarity with regulated industries such as financial services, healthcare, or insurance
• Production experience with agentic systems or AI-integrated workflows.
• Contributions to a shared platform or open source project that others built on.

(Remote, US East Coast or the same time zone. Series B. DevTools SaaS. Synthetic monitoring. 40h/week)
The best developers don’t wait for a customer to tell them something’s broken.
They catch it first, in the pull request, in staging, or in the checkout flow at 3am, before a single user notices. That instinct is Checkly’s whole reason to exist. Now that agents write and ship more and more code, they can carry that instinct too. Agents write, run, and maintain the monitoring setup that guards production, while developers stay in control. Everything is defined as code, powered by OpenTelemetry and Playwright, and versioned and reviewed like everything else that ships. From pull request to post-mortem, in one place.
AI agents are shipping more code than any team can review, and reliability is lagging behind. Checkly closes this gap. As a Support Engineer, you’ll support our most valuable customers, from modern AI companies like Mistral and resolve.ai to large engineering orgs like LinkedIn, Citi, and 1Password on that journey.
In 2024 we raised $20M in Series B funding from Balderton, CRV and Accel. We’re a remote-first startup that is low on meetings, high on productivity, and always shipping. If you love actually listening to and working with customers, working async, and keeping it lean, you’ll fit right in!
We care about building a team where people of all backgrounds are encouraged to do their best work. To achieve this we built a flexible and async-first startup environment with inclusive benefits and full transparency about how we pay.
## What you’ll do
Support has always been about solving real problems for real people. What’s changing at Checkly is how we do it: AI lets us automate routine work and assist us with troubleshooting, so we can go deeper on hard cases and bring what customers tell us straight back to the product. Here’s where you come in:
• Resolve customer issues. Debug Playwright tests (flaky selectors, timeouts, auth flows). Dig into API check failures with packet captures (PCAPs), traceroutes and timing breakdowns. Set up single sign-on (SSO) and SAML. When it’s a bug, bring engineering a clean reproduction, or open the pull request (PR) yourself.
• Build an outstanding AI support process. Our internal and external support agents already resolve 80% of tickets. You’ll help lift the bar: what the agent answers, when it hands off to a human, and how good those answers are.
• Turn tickets into product. Spot patterns across customers and bring product and engineering a reproduction. Your work becomes bug fixes and features.
• Own the docs. If you’ve answered something twice, it belongs in the docs and in the agent, so customers and AI get the same right answer.
• Work with modern tooling. We are continuously updating our workbench, and you’ll have modern tools like Plain, Linear, and Mintlify.
## This won't be the right role if you...
• Want a clear process for every situation before you act.
• Would rather code all day than talk to customers.
• See AI tools as something you’ll get around to eventually.
• Want the structure and pace of a large company.
## What you should have
You will often speak with developers who need assistance understanding if their applications work well and if not, what caused the issue. This requires a solid technical background and a genuine motivation to help and learn.
• Empathy: You love working with customers and solving their problems. Checkly is critical to them, and we genuinely want to unblock them.
• Some experience in a technical role, for example, as a developer or in technical support.
• You can read and debug JavaScript, TypeScript and Node.js code.
• You’re comfortable with HTTP, REST APIs, browser dev tools, git and CI/CD practices.
• AI is already how you work. Claude Code, Codex, Cursor or similar are part of your day. You’ve built your own workflows.
• You write and speak clear, friendly English.
• You can run your own day remotely and still enjoy working with your team.
• You're based on the US East Coast or the same time zone.
## Why us?
• Transparent salary because your salary shouldn't be dictated by how good a negotiator you are. (more info below)
• Async-first (low meeting, high productivity) and transparent culture
• Stock options
• Flexible paid vacation
• Paid sick leave & up to 14 weeks of paid parental leave
• US: Medical, Dental, Vision, FSA, long- and short-term disability, life insurance, 401(k) and more
• Annual company off-site
Find out more here .
## What we pay
Fair, competitive, and transparent pay is very important for us. Therefore we work with a standardized salary calculator that includes several factors such as seniority level as well as location.
For this role, the range is
• $57,500 - $70,000 for someone in the US
• $71,910 - $87,000 for someone in US Tier 1 locations like NYC, Boston
• $43,000 - $52,000 for someone in e.g. South America
## Apply
If this sounds interesting, please apply! Studies by several different sources have shown that on average men will apply for a job if they meet 60% of the application requirements. Women, non-binary people and POC will seek to match a much higher percentage of requirements before applying. If you're not sure you're the right fit, apply anyway and let us know what you bring to the table. We'd love to hear from you!
We're all about being transparent and setting clear expectations. That's why we've put together our hiring playbook and open-sourced our employee handbook . There you'll find a sneak peek of who we are, how we work and what you can expect in our hiring process.

## Why Harvey
At Harvey, we’re transforming how legal and professional services operate. By combining frontier agentic AI, an enterprise-grade platform, and deep domain expertise, we’re reshaping how critical knowledge work gets done for decades to come.
This is a rare chance to help build a generational company at a true inflection point. We have strong product-market fit and world-class investor support. We’re scaling fast and defining a new category in real time. The work is ambitious, the bar is high, and the opportunity for growth — personal, professional, and financial — is unmatched.
Our team moves fast, takes ownership, and is deeply committed to the mission — operating with intensity, staying close to our customers, and pushing each other for excellence. We live by three values: Decisiveness, Simplicity, and Job's Not Finished. We act quickly on clear judgment over perfect information, we believe simplicity is what scales, and we're never satisfied with where we are. If you want to do the best work of your career alongside people who share that drive, we'd love to build with you.
At Harvey, the future of professional services is being written today — and we’re just getting started.
## Role Overview
We’re looking for a Senior People Systems Analyst to own and scale the systems and workflows that support Harvey’s growing global workforce. This role will primarily focus on Workday HCM, owning the design, configuration, testing, and continuous improvement of complex business processes. You’ll also be the go-to systems expert for Benefits and our Applicant Tracking System (Ashby). That means leading feature evaluation, solution design, configuration, root-cause troubleshooting, and end-to-end testing.
You’ll partner closely with People Operations, Benefits, Recruiting, Payroll, Finance, Legal, and Corporate IT to turn business needs into scalable, intuitive, and well-governed system solutions. The ideal candidate is an experienced, hands-on systems professional who works independently from requirements through deployment, brings a clear point of view on how to solve problems, and influences stakeholders toward durable, scalable outcomes.
## What You'll Do
• Own the configuration, maintenance, and optimization of Workday HCM, including complex business processes, condition rules, approval routing, notifications, security assignments, and worker lifecycle workflows.
• Lead solution design end to end: translate ambiguous business needs into system solutions, assess downstream impacts across HCM, Benefits, Payroll, reporting, integrations, and employee experience, and bring recommendations to critical decision points.
• Serve as the subject-matter expert for Benefits systems, owning plan configuration, eligibility rules, enrollment workflows, vendor integrations, annual enrollment readiness, issue resolution, and process improvements.
• Support Recruiting Systems and administration which includes integrations, and data quality.
• Advise senior stakeholders on system capabilities, new features, configuration tradeoffs, and opportunities to simplify or automate manual processes. Explain complex topics clearly and persuasively.
• Define and drive testing strategy across Workday, Benefits, Ashby, and connected systems, including workflow, regression, release, and user acceptance testing.
• Diagnose complex or unusual system and data issues by tracing configuration, business rules, integrations, and upstream and downstream dependencies. Identify root causes and put durable fixes in place rather than one-off workarounds.
• Lead enhancement projects from discovery through deployment with People Operations, Benefits, Recruiting, Payroll, Finance, Legal, and IT, including gathering requirements, documenting options, and prioritizing work.
• Set the standard for configuration documentation, test plans, process maps, release notes, and operational procedures that support governance and team self-service.
• Proactively monitor system health and data integrity, lead audit and reconciliation support, and uphold security and data governance practices for employee and candidate data.
• Lead Workday and vendor release management: evaluate new functionality, assess impact, coordinate testing, and drive adoption decisions.
• Act as a resource for peers and stakeholders on complex or challenging systems questions, sharing knowledge and best practices across the team.
## What You Have
• 5+ years of hands-on experience configuring and supporting Workday, an HRIS, or related enterprise business systems.
• Deep experience with Workday HCM configuration and the Business Process Framework, including condition rules, approval routing, notifications, security, and workflow design.
• Proven ability to independently design and deliver complex, cross-system workflows, using sound judgment to know when a decision needs broader review.
• A track record of owning projects that improved workflows, reduced manual effort, or introduced new tools or automation.
• Strong experience turning ambiguous business requirements into system solutions, often with limited information, and explaining technical tradeoffs persuasively to non-technical and senior audiences.
• Experience defining and running testing strategies, including regression, UAT, defect triage, data validation, and production change management.
• Solid working knowledge of Benefits administration or Benefits systems, including eligibility, enrollment, plan configuration, vendor feeds, and annual enrollment.
• Advanced analytical and problem-solving skills, with the ability to identify root causes across systems, processes, integrations, and data.
• Excellent communication, documentation, and stakeholder management skills, adapting your style to different audiences.
• Ability to manage competing priorities independently, make well-reasoned recommendations, and operate effectively in a fast-moving, high-growth environment.
## Bonus Points
• Workday certification or Workday Pro certification in HCM, Benefits, or a related area.
• Experience with Workday integrations, EIBs, reports, calculated fields, or APIs.
• Experience supporting recruiting system integrations with Workday or other people systems.
• Experience with Workday Benefits, Absence, Compensation, Payroll, or Recruiting-related processes.

Healthcare is in crisis and the people behind the results deserve better. With more and more data coming from wearables, lab tests, and patient–doctor interactions, we’re entering an era where data is abundant.
Junction is building the infrastructure layer for diagnostic healthcare, making patient data accessible, actionable, and automated across labs and devices. Our mission is simple but ambitious: build the infrastructure that makes predictive, personalized care possible.
If you're passionate about how technology can supercharge healthcare, you’ll fit right in.
Backed by Creandum, Point Nine, 20VC, YC , and leading angels, we’re working to solve one of the biggest challenges of our time: making healthcare personalized, proactive, and affordable. We’re already connecting millions and scaling fast.
## Short on time? TL;DR:
• You: An integration or implementation specialist who can write and ship your own code. You’ve worked closely with partners and technology to move things along, you reach for tools like Claude or Codex to build your own solutions, and you’d rather automate a process than repeat it.
• Us: A team of ~60 connecting digital health companies to labs like Quest and LabCorp.
## Why we need you
Getting a new customer live with one of our lab partners means proving that their data is landing in our system exactly right. We’re doing that for about 30 accounts at once, with no sign of it slowing down. Nobody owns this fully today. You'll be the first person to take it end-to-end and build the automation that makes it basically run itself.
Certification is the first problem we need you to solve, but it’s not the last: across 20+ lab partners, there’s a similar list of manual processes waiting for the same treatment, and they’re yours to turn into real integrations and automations.
You’ll have genuine license to build, with AI as your main lever, working alongside Oliver and Andy , and closely with Jeff . For the right person, it’s a strong first step into solutions engineering.
## What you'll be doing day to day
• Own lab certifications end-to-end: pick up new requests from Quest and LabCorp, build the test plan, run the cases, and get each account over the line.
• Keep ~30 moving at once: know where every certification stands and chase whatever is stuck without being asked.
• Be the go-to person for our lab partners: reliable, organized back-and-forth with Quest, LabCorp, and our other partners on test cases and issues.
• Push the automation further: a lot of certification work today is still manual, and we expect most of the happy path to be automated within the next year. You’ll be the one building that — with scripts, agents, whatever cuts the manual work — not just running the process by hand.
• Get hands-on with the data: dig into our backend, databases, and API responses when a result doesn’t land the way it should — in practice this means running scripts yourself (sandbox overrides, Quest order pulls, HL7 changes), not flagging it for someone else to fix.
• Run the other partner processes: set up lab accounts and sub-accounts, track pricing requests, and make sure our team always knows where things stand.
• Keep customers informed: maintain the docs that explain certification and account setup to customers and our sales team.
• Find the next process to fix: spot other lab workflows that are manual and repetitive, and make the case for automating them.
## What success looks like
• Every certification and partner process has a clear owner, status, and next step. Nobody has to ask where things stand.
• Accounts go live faster, with less back-and-forth with our partners.
• At least one more lab partner process has moved out of a spreadsheet or inbox and into something that mostly runs itself.
## What we're looking for
• Implementation or integrations experience: 2+ years running implementations, integrations, or technical support for an API-based or similarly technical product.
• Ecosystem thinking: you've worked somewhere with an active network of partners and integrations, not just a customer and a vendor. You understand that improving a process with a lab partner affects our customer and our customer's customer.
• Technically minded: you can make code changes and ship fixes yourself — in a script, a database query, or an API integration — without needing an engineer to review your work line by line. You don’t need to be an engineer, but you need real coding ability, not just comfort reading code.
• Hands-on scripting: you’re comfortable writing SQL and scripting in Python or JavaScript — this is how you’ll actually get the job done.
• AI-native: you already use AI tools every day and have built them into your workflows. When something is repetitive, AI is the first thing you reach for.
• Project management: you can keep dozens of things moving at once without anything slipping.
• High ownership: you see a problem and want to solve it next. The best person for this role looks at the manual work and decides it shouldn't need a human.
• Dependable with partners: you're clear, organized, and responsive with outside contacts, and you'll represent Junction with our lab partners.
• Nice to have: experience with lab or healthcare data (HL7, results interfaces, EMRs), SQL, or scripting in Python or JavaScript.
You don't need to tick every box to fit in here. If the problems we're solving genuinely interest you and you know you can contribute, we'd love to talk.
## What this role isn't
• You're looking for a customer success role: you'll talk to customers when it helps get them live, but most of your time is with lab partners and our internal teams.
• You want a pure engineering role: you'll work with code and data, but the job is owning a process and automating it, not shipping product. With that said, this isn’t a role where you can avoid code — you’ll be writing and shipping changes yourself, just not building product features.
• You're happy doing the same task the same way forever: certification is repetitive by nature, and your job is to make it less so.
• You want a fully defined playbook: our tooling is a strong start, but how far we take it is up to you.

We're on a mission to make the world's information accessible to everyone , regardless of the language they speak. ## What is Loancrate?
We started Loancrate to make home-buying simpler and less expensive for lenders and borrowers. Today, mortgage lenders are stuck running their companies on software products built 20 years ago. These products are slow, unstable, and don't lead to material improvements in efficiency. When using these systems, the average human cost to originate a loan is still over $11,000.
Loancrate builds AI-native tooling to automate mortgage workflows. Our ultimate goal is fully automated origination, which has the potential to save lenders over $16B in operating expense per year.
Since starting in 2020, our remote team has enabled our customers to power >$85 billion in new home loans. We care about collaboration, very open communication covering the good & the bad so that we learn from our decisions quickly, and ultimately having fun while we're building. You'll fit in well if you like diving deep quickly!
## The Opportunity

## What is Loancrate?
We started Loancrate to make home-buying simpler and less expensive for lenders and borrowers. Today, mortgage lenders are stuck running their companies on software products built 20 years ago. These products are slow, unstable, and don't lead to material improvements in efficiency. When using these systems, the average human cost to originate a loan is still over $11,000.
Loancrate builds AI-native tooling to automate mortgage workflows. Our ultimate goal is fully automated origination, which has the potential to save lenders over $16B in operating expense per year.
Since starting in 2020, our remote team has enabled our customers to power >$85 billion in new home loans. We care about collaboration, very open communication covering the good & the bad so that we learn from our decisions quickly, and ultimately having fun while we're building. You'll fit in well if you like diving deep quickly!
## The Opportunity
Buying a new loan origination system is the easy part. Actually configuring it to match how a lender runs its business - their conditions, their disclosures, their underwriting guidelines, their quirks - is where implementations are won or lost. We're looking for an Implementation Consultant to be the person in the room (virtually or on-site) who makes that configuration work actually happen.
This is a forward-deployed, hands-on role. You'll work directly with a lender's team during the implementation phase to configure Loancrate around their workflows, answer their configuration questions, and get them through user acceptance testing. Once the customer is live, you roll off and move to the next implementation - the CSM stays on as the long-term relationship owner, and the Implementation Lead keeps the overall project plan on track, while you're the one actually in the product with the customer making it work.
Because this role sits inside an active mortgage workflow from day one, you need to already be fluent in mortgage - not learning it as you go. We can teach you Loancrate inside and out. What we can't do in any reasonable timeframe is teach you what a lender's processors and underwriters actually need a system to do for them.
This is a foundational role on a team we're building from scratch: you'll help define what "good configuration" looks like, build the muscle memory for how we implement lenders quickly and correctly, and be one of the people whose work most directly determines whether a customer's go-live goes smoothly.
## What You'll Do
• Act as the forward-deployed implementation expert - work directly with the customer's team to configure Loancrate around their specific workflows, conditions, and business rules.
• Translate a lender's current-system setup into a Loancrate configuration - take how they operate today and recommend (and build) the configuration that gets them the same outcome, or better, in Loancrate.
• Own testing support during UAT - respond to configuration and testing questions as they come in, and work the "UAT Blocked" queue in Jira so customer-reported blockers get resolved quickly instead of sitting.

Managed Kubernetes across the major clouds. On-premises and fully air-gapped clusters with no route to the internet, GPU infrastructure, self-hosted model serving. Customer HPC environments, schedulers, and shared storage under real load.

We’re backed by Walmart, the world’s largest retailer, and Ribbit Capital, one of fintech’s most respected investors, giving us rare scale, distribution, and the opportunity to build something truly category-defining.
But what really sets OnePay apart is how we move. Our customers don’t have time to wait… and neither do we. This place moves fast, and we’re looking for people who are:
• Ready to run
• Hungry and driven by urgency
• Exceptional at what they do, with low ego
• Comfortable operating in motion
## The Role
Our growth stack has a lot of moving parts. The app and the website send events through a customer data platform to the ad platforms, our mobile measurement partners and the data warehouse. Most launches touch several of those systems and a few different teams.
You'll own the growth roadmap and work day to day with the MarTech and growth engineers who build and maintain all of this. Your job is to keep launches moving, make sure they get properly tested, and make sure the numbers on the other side can be trusted.
## What You'll Do
• Own the growth roadmap. Turn requests from marketing, paid media and product into scoped tickets with clear owners and dates. Keep the roadmap, runbooks and data flow docs current, and automate the repetitive parts with scripts or AI tools.
• Lead testing and QA with the MarTech and growth engineers. Write test plans, check changes in staging and on test devices before they ship, and confirm they worked after launch.
• Keep data flowing into paid media. Manage customer data platform destinations, audience syncs, reverse ETL and server-side events. Watch for dropped events, low match rates and schema drift, and write or tweak simple scripts when a setting isn't enough.
• Own our relationship with the mobile measurement partners. Debug attribution problems, keep SDK and ad network integrations healthy, and handle support escalations, renewals and roadmap requests.
• Keep tracking specs consistent across the app, the website, the customer data platform and web analytics, and dig in when numbers from different sources don't match.
• Run SDK upgrades, attribution migrations and new vendor onboarding from evaluation through cutover, with a rollback plan.
• Support paid and acquisition work across search, social, app-install networks, app store search ads and affiliates, including click ID plumbing, exclusion lists and test setup.
• Bring Privacy and Legal in early, so consent, data-sharing limits and data subject requests are part of the plan and not a surprise at launch.
## You Bring
• 8+ years in technical program management, supporting growth, performance marketing, martech or data teams.
• Hands-on time with a customer data platform. You've connected it to several ad platforms, mapped and filtered events, and synced audiences with consent rules applied. You can read a tracking plan or a destination config and spot where a launch will break.
• Experience with a mobile measurement partner and a good grasp of attribution: click IDs, ATT and SKAdNetwork, view-through versus click-through, and platform-reported versus first-party conversions. You've debugged discrepancies and dealt with the vendor directly.
• Experience doing testing and QA with engineers on tracking or integration launches: test plans, staging checks, debug tools, test devices, and regression checks after SDK or release changes.
• You write SQL and pull your own numbers.
• A track record of running programs across engineering, design, data and marketing, with clear specs, honest status updates and a written record of decisions.
• Good judgment on priorities, and comfort saying no. You're fine with ambiguity and with working asynchronously on a remote-first team.
## Nice to Have
• Experience at a consumer fintech or another regulated company.
• Reverse ETL into paid media (conversion APIs, offline conversions, audience uploads) and keeping it healthy: match rates, deduplication, delays and dropped events.
• Reading and writing simple scripts in JavaScript or Liquid, for example to transform an event payload or build a template.
• Experience with a cloud data warehouse.
• A working understanding of marketing privacy rules: consent, CCPA and similar state laws, GLBA, and limits on sharing customer data with ad platforms. You know when to ask Legal.

• A fixed fee per course is agreed upfront, based on course length and topic complexity. Fees are competitive, and advanced topics and exceptional instructors are paid accordingly. Payment is made on delivery of the completed course.

• Clear, engaging spoken English and confidence on camera.
• Openness to an established teaching methodology and to editorial feedback.
Nice to have

• Experience with fine-tuning, MLOps or deploying models in production.
• Cloud ML certifications (AWS, Azure, GCP, Databricks ).

Send your CV or LinkedIn profile, plus a link that shows how you teach: a course, a talk, a tutorial or a short video.

We are building AI to simulate the world through merging art and science.
We believe that world models are at the frontier of progress in artificial intelligence. Language models alone won’t solve the world’s hardest problems – robotics, disease, scientific discovery. Real progress requires models that experience the world and learn from their mistakes, the same way that humans do. And this kind of trial and error can be massively accelerated when done in simulation, rather than in the real world.
World models offer the most clear path to general-purpose simulation, changing how stories are told, how scientific progress is made and how the next frontiers of humanity are reached.
Our team consists of creative, open minded, caring and ambitious people who are determined to change the world. We aspire to continuously build impossible things and our ability to do so relies on building an incredible team. If you are driven to do the same, we'd love to hear from you.
*Titles posted to our careers page are updated regularly to best advertise the role and expected seniority, but internally we have a flat titling system with two types of titles: one for individual contributors and one for people managers.
## Why this matters
Runway is building AI to simulate the world. We think world models, not language models alone, are the path to general-purpose simulation: systems that experience the world, learn from their mistakes, and change how stories get told, how science gets done, and how the next frontiers of humanity are reached.
Applied AI is where that research meets a customer with a deadline. Every one of the world's largest studios, brands, and platforms hits a moment where Runway stops being a demo and becomes the way they actually make things. Our team exists for that moment, and we organize around one question: what's blocking this customer from production, and how do we remove it?
## About the role
This is a role for people who want to own a problem, not an account. You'll sit with the biggest studios, brands, and Fortune 100 companies in the world, figure out what's actually standing between them and production, and build whatever removes it. Some weeks that's a workflow. Some weeks it's a plugin or an integration nobody has written yet. Some weeks it's getting a room of executives to make a decision they've been putting off.
Your work will be on screen: Emmy-winning shows, Oscar-winning films, Super Bowl commercials, the stuff people actually watch. And the things you build for one customer tend to become product for all of them. Our team's first Shopify plugin started as a customer blocker and was in engineering's hands within a few weeks. We treat this team as R&D for that reason, not as a cost center.
We have offices in NYC, San Francisco, Seattle, and London.
## No two weeks are the same, but you can expect to:
• Find the real problem: sit with the creative, technical, and executive teams at a customer, map how they actually work, and locate the blocker between them and production. Usually it's one of three things: a missing integration, an unproven pipeline, or a stakeholder who isn't convinced yet.
• Build the first of its kind: the demo that shows a studio head or a Fortune 100 CMO something nobody has shown them before. Working proofs of concept on the customer's own brand, footage, or catalog, often built in a day or two before the meeting, and the best of them become product for everyone.
• Make it reusable: turn the one-off that unblocked one customer into the workflow, plugin, or integration the next ten customers start from.
• Run the evaluation: own evaluation plans end to end, guide managed trials, build tailored demos on the customer's own footage and brand, and carry the technical side of deal cycles with AEs.
• Scope deployments that land: 4–12 week engagements with customer-defined success criteria, a hands-on builder and an executive sponsor on their side from day one, and enough discipline to keep them on scope when the asks start piling up.
• Get customers to production fast: take new technical and non-technical customers from signed contract to first production call in days rather than quarters, grow API-only accounts into Platform + API, and fix the onboarding so the support tickets stop coming.
• Present to anyone: walk an analyst through a pipeline in the morning and a studio head through a production plan in the afternoon.
• Bring the field back to the product: embed with Product, Engineering, and Creative to turn what you saw at the customer into roadmap. Every repeat ask is a product requirement, not a patch.
• Measure what the customer measures: time to production, usage before and after a project, what they shipped because you were there. We track our own numbers in Salesforce and the warehouse; you'll own yours.
## What we value
• People who aren't satisfied with surface-level answers and will go into the data, the code, and the room to find the real one
• Low ego: the customer's outcome matters more than who gets the credit
• Comfort with open-ended problems in unstructured environments, and the instinct to create structure instead of waiting for it
• Builders who would rather prototype than debate, and who keep iterating with the customer until it actually works
• Adaptive and introspective: willing to learn, guide, lead, and follow
## What we need
• You build things that run in production. Python or TypeScript, APIs, integrations, and data pipelines. Whether you write the code yourself or with coding agents, you can read it, debug it when it breaks, and explain line by line why it's built that way, including to a customer's engineering team. You've shipped something a customer actually ran: a workflow, an integration, a plugin, or an internal tool.

## About the Role

Our mobile app is built in React Native and ships on both iOS and Android. Much of that work will be done in TypeScript and Node.js, so this role is a good fit for someone who enjoys writing code, debugging, and building tools. Because there’s no established QA team yet, you’ll work closely with the engineering team and have real influence shaping how we test, what tools we use, and how quality is measured.

• Perform exploratory testing to uncover edge cases, device and OS-version differences, and usability issues

• Begin building automated UI/UX regression tests for our React Native app
• Develop test fixtures and mock services in TypeScript and Node.js that simulate POS terminal behavior, reducing our reliance on physical hardware

• Partner with engineers and product managers during project planning, standups, and release readiness reviews

## Nice to Have

• Familiarity with bug tracking and test management tools (e.g., Jira, TestRail)
• Familiarity with API tools like Postman

• Familiarity with CI/CD tools (e.g., GitHub Actions, Jenkins, Bitrise, EAS)
## What You’ll Learn and Grow Into
• Designing a scalable React Native UI automation framework from the ground up
• Building mocks, simulators, and test fixtures for hardware and payment integrations in a production-quality Node.js and TypeScript codebase
• Understanding how React Native apps interact with native iOS and Android layers, and where platform-specific bugs come from

## About the Role
The Customer Onboarding Manager owns every new customer's path from the first handoff by our GTM (Go-To-Market) team to the day the customer is live in production. Your job is to make that path shorter, more predictable, and easier for the customer.
Today, the slowest part of a deal comes after the first sales conversation. Customers need internal approvals before a POC (Proof of Concept) can start: security questionnaires, compliance reviews, infrastructure and architecture questions, and procurement steps. Most of the delay sits on the customer's side, and some sits on ours. You will close both gaps.
You join the customer from the first call, build a shared onboarding plan, and track every open item until it is done. You chase approvals on the customer's side and pull in the right people on ours: GTM, TPM (Technical Project Management), Security, Compliance, and Infrastructure. You do not answer deep technical questions yourself; you make sure the right expert answers them on time.
You will also find the patterns behind the delays and fix them, turning one-off efforts into a repeatable onboarding process.

End-to-End Onboarding Ownership
• Take the handoff from GTM and join customer calls from the start of each engagement.
• Build a shared onboarding plan with each customer covering security review, compliance review, infrastructure questions, procurement, POC, and production go-live.
• Own the timeline, open items, and next steps for several customer onboardings at the same time.
• Keep the customer and internal teams aligned on what is done, what is blocked, and who owns each next step.
Customer-Side Approvals
• Map each customer's internal approval path early: who signs off on security, compliance, architecture, legal, and procurement.
• Follow up consistently with customer stakeholders to keep approvals moving.
• Help customers get what their reviewers need, such as completed questionnaires, compliance evidence, and architecture documents.
• Spot stalled approvals early and escalate through the right customer and Tessera contacts.
Internal Coordination
• Route customer questions to the right Tessera team (TPM, Security, Compliance, Infrastructure, or GTM) and track them to a committed answer date.
• Make sure handoffs between teams happen without dropped items or repeated questions to the customer.
• Identify internal gaps that slow onboarding, such as missing documents, slow answers, or unclear ownership, and drive fixes with the owning team.
Process and Reporting
• Build and maintain a repeatable onboarding playbook, including stage definitions, checklists, templates, and handoff criteria.
• Track onboarding metrics, such as time from GTM handoff to POC start and from POC to production, and report trends to leadership.
• Keep a reusable library of common customer requests and answers with the owning teams so later onboardings move faster.
• Use AI tools to speed up tracking, follow-ups, and reporting.
## What We're Looking For
• 3–5 years of experience in customer onboarding, implementation management, customer success, project coordination, or a similar customer-facing role at a B2B (business-to-business) software company.
• Excellent written and verbal communication, with the confidence to lead calls with customer stakeholders and follow up without being prompted.
• A record of running several customer engagements at once and keeping each one on schedule.
• Experience building processes from scratch, such as playbooks, checklists, and trackers, and getting other teams to use them.
• Strong organization and follow-through, with a habit of clear written status updates.
• Basic understanding of what enterprise security reviews, compliance requirements, and cloud deployments involve. You need to understand the questions well enough to route them; you do not need to answer them.
• Comfort working across teams where you have influence but not direct authority.

Tonic.ai has been de-identifying sensitive data since 2018, and hundreds of enterprises use our products, among them eBay, American Express, UnitedHealth Group, Volvo, Qualcomm, and Commonwealth Bank. Most of them came to us with the same problem: their engineers need realistic data to build and test software, and they can’t use production data to do it.
We’re looking for someone who loves to solve complex customer problems and then immediately turns around and builds a system so that this problem solves itself next time. Moreover, this person gets to the root of why and how each customer is using Tonic so that they can maximize the value every customer is getting out of our product. The ideal Solutions Architect will be proactive, coming up with creative solutions if customers aren't getting what they need, and pressing customers when they're not doing what they need to succeed.
## Why This Role, Why Now
AI has made writing code nearly free. Knowing whether that code, and the agents built on top of it, will behave in production hasn’t gotten any easier. Agents especially need realistic, messy, data to be tested against, and basic solutions / AI slop won’t surface the failures that matter. Teams are shipping faster than their test data can keep up, and that gap is our business.
The platform is robust and scalable. What makes it valuable is someone who can walk into a customer’s environment, work out where Tonic fits in their stack and their release process, prove it in a pilot, and make it stick after the deal closes. That’s this job. You’ll work alongside our AEs before the sale and with customers’ engineering teams after it, with a direct line back to our product and engineering teams.
## What You’ll Do
• Run technical discovery with prospects’ engineering, DevOps and QA teams. Map their data sources, environments and release process, and find where Tonic fits.
• Design and demo the solution, and handle the hard technical questions: security review, deployment model, performance at scale, and how Tonic fits their CI/CD.
• Scope pilots with clear, written success criteria, then run them to a decision.
• Own onboarding after the deal closes. Deploy Tonic, connect data sources, configure de-identification and subsetting, and get the customer generating usable test data within our time-to-generation targets.
• Design test-data pipelines for agent and software testing, combining de-identified production data and synthetic data to fit each customer’s environment.
• Diagnose problems as they appear: broken foreign keys, schema drift, sensitive columns missed, jobs that won’t finish. Fix them where you can. Where you can’t, understand the issue well enough to explain it clearly to the engineer who can.
• Train customer teams so they can run Tonic without you.
• Bring field insight back to product and engineering: which features matter, which bugs are blocking deals and where the product should go next.
• Support existing customers on high-complexity issues, and work with account teams to spot expansion early.
• Turn every one-off fix into something reusable: scripts, documentation, runbooks and product improvements, so each SA can support more customers than the last.
## What We’re Looking For
• A bachelor’s degree in a technical field (computer science, engineering, information systems, math or similar), or equivalent experience.
• 3+ years in a technical customer-facing role: Solutions Architect, Sales Engineer, Technical Customer Success or Forward Deployed Engineer.
• Hands-on experience with relational databases and data warehouses, and with cloud infrastructure (AWS, Azure or GCP). You can read a schema and tell quickly where the trouble will be.
• Working knowledge of how modern software gets built and tested: CI/CD, Docker and Kubernetes, test environments and testing frameworks.
• Comfort scripting and automating in Python and SQL. You’d rather build the fix than repeat the workaround.
• AI-native workflow. AI tools and agents are central to how you work. You know where they’re reliable and where they need your oversight.
• Ownership. You’ll often be the technical lead on an account, making sound calls without waiting to be told.
• Range. You can go deep with a DBA on one call and make the business case to a VP of Engineering on the next.
• Willingness to travel up to 25%, domestic and international.
## Nice to Haves
• Experience with agent evaluation and testing.
• Experience with test data management, data masking, or synthetic data tooling.
• Experience supporting security and compliance reviews in regulated industries like healthcare and financial services.
• Experience at an early-stage company or on a new product line.
## What Success Looks Like
In your first month, you’ll learn the platform and the delivery process and run pre- and post-sale engagements alongside your peers. By the end of your first quarter, you’ll run engagements on your own, and the scripts and runbooks you’ve written will have made your third onboarding faster than your first. After that, it’s about execution: converting pilots into customers and getting them live on time. You’ll also help shape how the SA function scales as we grow.
## Why Join
• You’ll be early in agent testing, a market that’s taking shape right now, working with some of the largest companies in the world.
• You’ll see an unusually wide range of technical environments, from startups to the Fortune 500 and from cloud-native stacks to mainframes.
• You’ll have a direct line from what you see in the field to what gets built.
• You’ll help define how the next generation of software and agents gets tested.
• Competitive compensation and equity.

## About WeTravel

About the Role
Clutch builds AI agents that work on behalf of credit unions. Emma, our collections agent, is live at five credit unions and handled 60,000+ member conversations in her first twelve weeks at one of them. Behind her is a growing portfolio: origination, fraud step-up, member (re)engagement and activation agents, all built on the same Agents Platform (TypeScript, NestJS, our own agent SDK, MCP, Temporal, promptfoo).
As a FDE you are one of the two engineers on an agent. You take it from "sold" to "live and performing" at a specific credit union: you sit in the discovery sessions, you build the integrations to their core banking and loan systems, you author and tune the agent's behavior, you run the live tests with their staff, and you stay with it through go-live and the first weeks of production. When something needs a person in the room, you are the one who flies.
This is a senior engineering role, not a solutions or support role. You write production code in our monorepo every week: integrations, modules, and the agents themselves (prompts, tools, evals), together with the other engineers on the pod. The difference from a traditional engineer is that you are on site more often, you make judgment calls in front of the customer, and you own the outcome. What you learn in the field flows straight back into the product: defaults, playbooks, and the platform capabilities the next agent will need.
You build; our AI Operations Managers deliver. The pod (pod lead plus engineers) designs and builds each agent in a high-touch way with the first customers. Once the agent is defined and live, AI Ops coordinates the implementations, configuration and ongoing success at the next credit unions. You hand them something that works and a playbook to run it.
• This role requires roughly 20% of travel on average, with one- to two-week stretches around kickoffs and go-lives. Based in the US, able to travel on short notice
About the Team
You'll join the Agents team, a small, senior group operating as a startup inside Clutch: seven engineers, a dedicated AI product group, and AI sales specialists, working directly with some of the largest credit unions in the country. Every agent is staffed by a pair of engineers, one leaning toward the conversation and LLM side, one toward software and integrations, with a pod lead who owns the product day to day. There is no layer between you and the customer, and no layer between you and the platform team.
The operating style is direct, written, and evidence-driven: BLUF updates, evals over opinions, business outcomes over ticket counts. The team is spread across Brazil, Argentina and the US and works async by default. Being on site is a tool we use at specific moments (kickoff, live testing, go-live), not a permanent posting.
What You’ll Do
Within 1 months, you will:
• Ship your first production change to a live agent through the team's review process, and be able to explain how a member's call flows through the Agents Platform end to end
• Learn one agent deeply: system prompt, tool contracts, orchestration triggers, compliance gates, and the implementation process from kickoff to go-live
• Join at least one credit union implementation as the second engineer, including a live testing session with their staff
• Map where the current implementation process loses time and where a default or a tool would have removed a round trip
Within 3 months, you will:
• Own the technical side of one credit union implementation end to end: core and LOS integration, agent configuration, testing, go-live, and the first weeks of production
• Run the eval and tuning loop for your agent (golden transcripts, rubric judges, regression suite) and be trusted to change its behavior without a second engineer checking your work
• Have completed at least two on-site visits and turned what you heard there into product decisions with your pod lead and PM
• Contribute at least one reusable capability back to the Agents Platform that the next implementation will not have to rebuild
Within 6 months, you will:
• Have taken one net-new agent from sold to live at its first credit union, with data you can show the partner
• Be the engineer credit union staff ask for by name when something in their deployment needs to change
• Have written the implementation playbook for your agent well enough that the AI Ops team runs the second and third credit union without you
• Be shaping what the next agents look like, because you have seen where the current ones break in the field
What You’ll Bring
In rough priority order.
• 7+ years of software engineering in a fast-paced environment, preferably in SaaS and/or Fintech, with senior TypeScript and Node.js backend experience in a large codebase (NestJS, CQRS, schema-validated boundaries, dependency injection). We do not count years of AI experience; the field is too young for that to mean anything. We look at what you have shipped and how you reason about it
• Integration and API engineering: secure service-to-service endpoints, third-party APIs, webhooks, and the patience to work with legacy banking systems that were not designed to be integrated
• Security and auth judgment: OAuth and machine-to-machine auth, tenant-scoped access, secrets handling, no PII in logs. Our agents touch sensitive member data and operate under consumer-contact regulation
• Customer presence: you can sit across from a VP of Collections, hear a request, and say "here is what I recommend and why", including when the answer is no. You are comfortable making calls in the room and owning them afterwards

• Genuine appetite for LLM agents: eval discipline for non-deterministic systems, reading a system prompt like code, understanding that some decisions must never reach the model. Curiosity plus shipped work is enough; research depth is not required
• Nice to have, explicitly not required: voice and telephony (LiveKit, Twilio), Temporal or event-driven orchestration, Python, core banking or LOS integration experience, credit union or banking domain knowledge

## About Medley Learning
Medley is an instructional support tool for multilingual learners that helps students access grade-level content. Our browser extension layers individualized reading and writing scaffolds directly onto the digital materials schools already use, including curriculum platforms, Google Docs, websites, and PDFs. Supports are tailored to a student's English proficiency level and home language, so students get the help they need in real time while staying engaged with the same rigorous content as their peers. Medley is grounded in research-backed practices and is already being used by over 50 districts across the US.
## The Opportunity
We're hiring a Technical Product Manager, Pedagogy & AI Quality to ensure that Medley’s AI-powered instructional scaffolds continue to meet our high bar for quality and user experience. You'll tighten our rubrics for what high-quality scaffolds look like for reading and writing support in the areas of both multilingual learning and special education, and across various subjects. You’ll expand upon our metrics, build upon our robust evals systems, and review processes that hold our AI to that bar.
This is a hybrid role at the intersection of pedagogy and AI product work. You'll write and test prompts, label and analyze model outputs, dig through traces and error reports, and partner closely with engineering to ship quality improvements. You will also learn and leverage the research around scaffolding high-quality instructional materials for multilingual learners at different proficiency levels, as well as accommodations and supports for students with receptive and expressive language disabilities and neurodivergent students.
You'll work closely with our head of product and engineers to ensure that Medley consistently serves teachers and students in our partner districts with scaffolds that meet the highest levels of quality. Over time, you’ll own the quality and usability of our scaffolds suite as it continues to grow to support more students with diverse needs, prioritizing product improvements and new features to better support teachers and drive student outcomes.
## What You'll Do
• Define what "excellent" looks like. Translate research-based practice in literacy, special education, and multilingual learner instruction into clear, usable quality standards for Medley scaffolds, and set targets for AI output quality.
• Track and monitor quality with a robust evals system. Build and maintain datasets, rubrics, and eval suites and conduct regular error analysis and trace review, combining human labeling, LLM-as-judge and rule-based evals.
• Refine prompts and models as needed. Write, test, and refine prompts; run model comparisons and regression tests, making changes as needed to ensure outputs are consistently meeting target metrics and passing quality thresholds.
• Stay close to our users and represent their voice in product decisions. Regularly review signals from educators, data from support tickets, product analytics, and conduct user research with students and teachers to inform product decisions.
• Prioritize and ship AI quality and scaffold-related product improvements. Maintain a prioritized backlog of AI quality and scaffold UX issues; write clear specs, and work with engineering to scope, build and verify fixes, product updates and new features.
## What We're Looking For
• Pedagogical expertise , especially in scaffolding literacy instruction for struggling readers, special education, and/or multilingual learner education, and ideally from classroom teaching, intervention, instructional coaching or curriculum design.
• Hands-on experience with AI evals , including human labeling, LLM-as-judge rubric design, AI metrics targets definition, and error analysis of LLM outputs.
• AI product fluency : you use LLMs daily and have experience designing complex AI systems for products.
• Experience defining new features and collaborating with engineers to deliver them : you can clearly communicate a problem and solution, and work through technical tradeoffs and UX questions.
• Strong initiative, sharp judgment, and clear writing : you take action when you spot a problem, make swift decisions grounded in data and instincts, and communicate clearly to both technical and non-technical audiences.
## Nice to Have
• Graduate degree and/or significant direct experience in special education, reading/literacy, ESL/ELD or bilingual education.
• Familiarity with AI eval and observability tools (e.g., LangSmith, Braintrust, Arize, Langfuse) or annotation platforms.
• Proficiency in a language other than English.
• Prior work at an edtech company, or on content quality, assessment design or psychometrics.
• Familiarity with accessibility standards (e.g., WCAG) and assistive technology.
## Why Join Medley
Medley is building products for multilingual learners and students with disabilities, populations that together represent more than 20% of U.S. K-12 students and have historically been underserved by edtech.
You'll join early, work directly with founders and engineering leadership, own meaningful technical and design decisions, and help shape a product that improves access to learning for students nationwide.
We are committed to creating a diverse and inclusive work environment. We welcome applicants from all backgrounds and experiences.

About the Role
mpathic provides independent, multidisciplinary evaluations of healthcare AI technologies seeking deployment in real-world clinical settings. As part of our work supporting Utah's Office of Artificial Intelligence Policy (OAIP) regulatory sandbox, we are recruiting experienced machine learning (ML) and data science professionals to serve as technical reviewers on expert evaluation panels.
In this role, you will independently assess the technical evidence supporting healthcare AI applications, including model performance, validation methodology, generalizability, reliability, and proposed monitoring and safeguards. Your assessments will help inform recommendations regarding whether and under what conditions an AI technology may be appropriate for pilot deployment.
You will work alongside clinical and other subject-matter experts to evaluate whether applicants' technical claims are supported by credible evidence and whether their proposed evaluation and monitoring plans are appropriate for the intended healthcare setting and patient population.
This is an evaluation and scientific review role, not a model development position. We are looking for experts who can critically assess existing evidence, identify limitations, and communicate actionable recommendations to technical and non-technical stakeholders.
What You'll Be Doing
Responsibilities may include:
• Evaluate model performance and validation: Assess the appropriateness of validation methods, reference standards, sample sizes, statistical analyses, performance metrics, operating thresholds, and reported uncertainty.
• Assess data quality and representativeness: Review whether training, testing, and validation datasets are appropriate for the intended clinical application, including potential data leakage, subgroup performance differences, and generalizability across patient populations and healthcare settings.
• Evaluate technical reliability: Assess evidence of model robustness, reproducibility, known failure modes, and performance under atypical or out-of-distribution inputs.
• Review proposed evaluation plans: Determine whether applicants have established scientifically defensible methods, performance benchmarks, and success criteria for evaluating AI technologies during pilot deployment, particularly when pre-deployment evidence is limited.
• Assess technical safeguards and human oversight: Evaluate whether proposed technical safeguards, escalation mechanisms, and human-in-the-loop processes are operationally feasible and supported by appropriate testing.
• Evaluate monitoring and change management: Assess applicants' plans for detecting performance degradation, monitoring model behavior, managing updates, and establishing criteria for intervention or rollback.
• Collaborate with multidisciplinary reviewers: Work alongside clinicians and other technical experts to identify concerns that require cross-disciplinary judgment, particularly where model performance may affect clinical outcomes.
• Produce structured evaluation findings: Document strengths, limitations, missing evidence, and technical concerns using a standardized review framework. Provide clear, evidence-based recommendations and identify what additional evidence or changes would resolve identified concerns.
• Participate in reviewer calibration and quality assurance: Contribute to discussions intended to improve consistency, transparency, and defensibility across evaluations.
• Maintain independence and confidentiality: Follow conflict-of-interest, confidentiality, and data-handling requirements when reviewing proprietary or unpublished materials.
What We're Looking For
We are seeking technically rigorous, independent reviewers who can distinguish between a promising technology and evidence that adequately supports its proposed use.
Strong candidates are comfortable questioning unsupported performance claims, identifying limitations in study design, and recognizing when additional evidence is needed before meaningful conclusions can be drawn. They understand that healthcare AI evaluation is context-dependent: technical performance must be considered alongside the intended population, clinical application, degree of autonomy, and potential consequences of model error.
Candidates should also be able to translate complex technical findings into clear, actionable recommendations for multidisciplinary audiences, including clinicians and state regulatory stakeholders.
Basic Qualifications
• At least 3 years of professional or applied research experience in machine learning, data science, biostatistics, clinical informatics, or a closely related field, with direct experience evaluating or validating predictive models or AI systems.
• Demonstrated understanding of model evaluation methodologies, including appropriate performance metrics, validation design, statistical uncertainty, threshold selection, and common sources of bias or methodological error.
• Experience assessing model performance on independent or held-out data and interpreting whether reported performance generalizes beyond the evaluation dataset.
• Hands-on experience evaluating at least one relevant class of AI systems, such as clinical natural language processing, large language models, conversational AI, medical imaging, computer vision, or tabular predictive models.
• Ability to critically assess technical research, evaluation reports, or validation studies and identify methodological limitations or unsupported conclusions.
• Strong analytical writing skills, including the ability to communicate complex findings clearly to non-technical audiences.
• Ability to work independently while contributing to multidisciplinary expert review and calibration processes.
• Willingness to complete confidentiality agreements, conflict-of-interest disclosures, and reviewer training requirements.
Preferred Qualifications
• Experience evaluating AI or ML systems used in healthcare, clinical decision support, digital health, or other high-stakes environments.
• Familiarity with clinical AI evaluation and reporting frameworks, such as TRIPOD+AI, STARD-AI, CONSORT-AI, DECIDE-AI, or model cards.
• Experience evaluating generative AI, LLM-based systems, or autonomous AI agents, including multi-turn behavior, reliability, hallucinations, and technical safeguards.
• Experience with robustness testing, adversarial evaluation, red teaming, or systematic failure-mode analysis.
• Knowledge of production monitoring, distribution shift, model drift, version control, and change-management practices.
• Experience designing or evaluating human-in-the-loop systems or comparing model performance against human expert judgments.
• Familiarity with FDA guidance for AI-enabled medical devices, clinical decision support, or software as a medical device.
• Experience conducting independent technical reviews, scientific peer reviews, grant reviews, or formal technology evaluations.

The Product Owner owns that end-to-end experience and the backlog that drives it.

## About the role:
Cresta’s AI Receptionist answers the phone for small businesses that would otherwise miss the call. It handles millions of conversations a month today, making sure no call goes unanswered and helping owners complete the front-office tasks that keep their business running, and it does so across hundreds of customers. Whether those conversations are actually good is the single most important question in the business, and it deserves a full-time owner. That’s you.
As our first AI Agent Evaluation Engineer, you define what quality means for every agent we run, you build the systems that measure it across every conversation, and you are the person the company trusts when the question is “how good is it, really?”
The work combines hands-on conversation analysis, rigorous evaluation design, and engineering execution: reading and annotating real conversations to learn how the agent actually fails, building the automated evaluation systems (LLM-based judges, golden sets, regression suites) that measure those failures at scale, and keeping those systems honest by calibrating them against human judgment. Fixing what you find is welcome but not the core of the job; an accurate, prioritized picture of agent quality is.
What You'll Do :
## Evaluation Design & Quality Definition
• Define and maintain the evaluation rubric for the agent across three axes: adherence (did it follow its design, call the right tools, respect guardrails), outcome (did the conversation achieve its goal), and conversation experience (latency, turn-taking, tone, repetition).
• Write the annotation guidelines and failure taxonomy the team uses to talk about failures precisely; run calibration sessions and measure inter-rater agreement.
• Classify and prioritize failure modes by severity and frequency so engineering and product work on what matters most.
## Conversation Analysis & Annotation
• Review production conversations by hand every week, leverage QA partners; open-code failures, cluster them, and turn the clusters into the evaluations worth automating.
• Trace each failure to its likely cause (prompt, knowledge gap, tool or flow bug, speech recognition) and route it to the right owner with enough evidence to act on.
• Evaluate across languages and report quality by segment (language, accent, audio quality, intent), not just in aggregate.
## Scalable Evaluation Systems
• Build and operate the evaluation pipeline that scores every production conversation, combining automated checks, LLM-based judges, and human review.
• Calibrate every automated judge against human labels before trusting it; treat judge error as the primary measurement risk.
• Design sampling strategies (stratified by intent, language, caller type, audio conditions) so that reported changes in quality are real.
• Build and maintain the golden set and regression suite that every prompt, model, knowledge, and flow change is validated against before release.
## Coverage & Edge Cases
• Maintain the failure-mode coverage map: which behaviors are tested, partially tested, or unmeasured; close the gaps.
• Design evaluations for behaviors no standard harness covers: high-stakes conversation types such as handoffs to a human, misuse and unwanted-caller handling, and resilience under upstream failures.
• Define the quality and latency thresholds the agent is held to.
## Reporting & Cross-Functional Collaboration
• Report quality trends to internal stakeholders and customers clearly, with uncertainty stated and without burying bad news.
• Partner with forward-deployed engineers, backend engineers, product managers, and the voice/language engineering team to turn findings into prioritized recommendations.
• Document methodology so results are reproducible and the evaluation practice outlives any one person.
## What We're Looking For:
• 3+ years of professional experience in software engineering, applied ML, or data-intensive research roles, including at least 1–2 years working hands-on with LLM-based systems in production.
• Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Computer Science, Computational Linguistics, Cognitive Science, Statistics, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience.
• Built and operated an end-to-end evaluation system for a production LLM product (agent or otherwise): rubric, human labels, automated judge, regression suite.
• Deep understanding of evaluation methodology: what golden sets, judges, regression suites, and calibration are for, and when each fails. Tool-agnostic; you will work in our in-house tooling.
• Fluent in how LLM agents work: prompts, tool calls, context handling, multi-turn state. You can read a trace and tell what the agent was doing and why.
• Strong programming skills in Python and experience with LLM APIs; able to build and ship evaluation tooling independently. Fine-tuning and ML frameworks are not required.
• Able to write a rubric that independent reviewers would score the same way, and to measure whether they do.
• Able to design a test from an open-ended quality question: you decide what to measure and how, rather than executing a predefined plan.
• Willing to do non-scalable work weekly, both yourself and by directing our QA partners: listening to calls, labeling conversations, building a failure taxonomy from scratch.
• Professional fluency in at least one language other than English, sufficient to evaluate multilingual agent behavior directly.
• Strong written communication; you author the guidelines others follow.
Note on Our Hiring Process
We highly value your time and engineering craftsmanship. Samsara (NYSE: IOT) is the pioneer of the Connected Operations™ Cloud, which is a platform that enables organizations that depend on physical operations to harness Internet of Things (IoT) data to develop actionable insights and improve their operations. At Samsara, we are helping improve the safety, efficiency and sustainability of the physical operations that power our global economy. Representing more than 40% of global GDP, these industries are the infrastructure of our planet, including agriculture, construction, field services, transportation, and manufacturing — and we are excited to help digitally transform their operations at scale.

At SentinelOne, we are driven by a clear purpose: to give the advantage to those who secure our future. As AI reshapes how organizations build, operate, and innovate, the responsibility to protect them becomes more critical than ever. When you join SentinelOne, your work helps protect global enterprises, critical infrastructure, and the technologies shaping tomorrow. If you are motivated by meaningful challenges and want your impact to be real, measurable, and global, you will find purpose here.
## About Us
SentinelOne is a company at the intersection of AI and security, pioneering a new operating model for cybersecurity. Our AI-native platform unifies protection across endpoint, cloud, identity, data, and AI systems to deliver autonomous detection and response with clarity and speed. By combining real-time analytics, intelligent automation, and a unified data foundation, we reduce noise, simplify complexity, and empower security teams to focus on what truly matters.
Our teams are builders, problem-solvers, and innovators committed to shaping the future of security. If you are excited to solve hard problems alongside talented, mission-driven people, we invite you to help us build a safer future for humanity.

We’re looking for people who are relentlessly curious and committed to continuous learning. AI is reshaping every function across our business, and we enable every team member, regardless of role or level, to build fluency in AI tools and concepts. Those who thrive here actively seek out new solutions, experiment thoughtfully, and apply what they learn to drive better, faster, smarter outcomes.
As a Technical Account Manager, you will be tasked with owning the overall relationship with SentinelOne's large-scale enterprise clients, leading complex implementation and onboarding projects, and delivering professional account management services that drive continued value and renewal. You'll work independently to evaluate customers' environments and architecture — including business needs, infrastructure, security, and compliance requirements — to deliver the right design and integration solution. You'll partner closely with Product, Engineering, Support, Sales, and leadership to advocate for customer needs, resolve technical and business issues, and identify growth opportunities. You're a fast learner and natural problem solver who thrives in a fluctuating workload, globally dispersed, cross-cultural team environment.

• Own the overall relationship with assigned large-scale clients, building the foundation for continued value growth and re-purchase loyalty toward SentinelOne's solutions.
• Lead complex implementation and onboarding projects for S1 products and services.
• Deliver professional and technical account management services — proactive communication, strategic advisory, technical project management, service reviews, escalation management, training, and more — following established best practices.
• Work independently to evaluate a customer's environment and architecture, delivering the right design and integration solution while maintaining high satisfaction.
• Collaborate with Product, Engineering, Support, Sales, and upper management to advocate for customer needs, resolve technical and business issues, define feature requests, and collect customer feedback.

• Maintain an in-depth understanding of company technology, products, and services.
• Contribute to the knowledge base by creating best-practice guides and video tutorials.

• At least 3 years of experience in field engineering: senior support engineer (tier 3–4), Technical Account Manager, or Pre-Sales.

• Multi-OS support experience across Windows, Mac, and Linux (mobile platform experience a plus).
• Required training delivery experience.
• Experience with Enterprise customers — required.
• MongoDB experience preferred; any prior database experience (queries and basic programming) is acceptable.
• Scripting experience, with at minimum a working knowledge of Python, PHP, and Unix shell scripts.
• A customer-oriented, professional, and articulate problem solver with excellent written communication skills.

AI is redefining how the world operates and rewriting the rules of security in real time, and SentinelOne was built for this moment.
