SingleStore is seeking a Forward Deployed Engineer (FDE) to operate at the intersection of solution architecture, technical delivery, and customer partnership. This role combines elements of a solutions architect, technical account manager, and solution engineer, with a strong emphasis on execution.
As an FDE, you will serve as a trusted technical advisor and sounding board for customers, helping them design, implement, and scale real-time data solutions using SingleStore. You will work closely with customers to understand their business objectives, translate them into technical strategies, and drive those solutions into production. This role requires a delivery mindset, strong technical depth, and the ability to lead both strategic conversations and hands-on execution.
Role and Responsibilities
• Partner directly with customers to understand their architecture, use cases, and business goals, and translate them into scalable technical solutions.
• Design and implement end-to-end solutions integrating SingleStore into existing application and data ecosystems.
• Lead whiteboard sessions to shape ideas, define architecture, and convert concepts into technical specifications and execution plans.
• Act as a proactive thought partner, bringing ideas and guiding conversations rather than reacting to requirements.
• Own delivery of high-impact initiatives from concept through production, ensuring successful outcomes.
• Provide hands-on support, including troubleshooting, optimization, and applying pragmatic solutions or fixes when needed.
• Collaborate closely with Sales, Solutions Engineering, Product, and Engineering teams to align customer needs with product capabilities and roadmap.
• Help customers prioritize and operationalize their data initiatives, balancing ambition with practical delivery.
• Feed insights from customer engagements back into Product and Engineering to influence roadmap and improvements.
## Your Experience
• 10+ years of experience in solution architecture, solution engineering, or technical consulting (pre-sales and/or post-sales).
• Strong foundation in databases, distributed systems, or software engineering.
• Proven experience delivering production-grade solutions in customer-facing environments.
• Experience integrating complex systems across data pipelines, applications, and infrastructure.
• Ability to translate ambiguous requirements into clear technical plans and drive execution.
• Experience working with enterprise customers, particularly in financial services or high-tech environments, is highly preferred.
• Strong communication and organizational skills, with the ability to guide both technical and non-technical stakeholders.
• Demonstrated ability to balance technical innovation with pragmatic delivery and realistic scoping.
• Alignment with product capabilities and roadmap, ensuring solutions are both impactful and feasible.
• This is a customer-facing role, and we prefer candidates based in the NYC area or within a commutable distance.
SingleStore delivers the cloud-native database with the speed and scale to power the world’s data-intensive applications. With a distributed SQL database that introduces simplicity to your data architecture by unifying transactions and analytics, SingleStore empowers digital leaders to deliver exceptional, real-time data experiences to their customers. SingleStore is venture-backed and headquartered in San Francisco with offices in Sunnyvale, Raleigh, Seattle, Boston, London, Lisbon, Bangalore, Dublin and Kyiv.
Consistent with our commitment to diversity & inclusion, we value individuals with the ability to work on diverse teams and with a diverse range of people.

## About Skylight
Skylight is a digital consultancy using design and technology to help government agencies deliver better public services.
We’re at the forefront of a civic movement to reinvent how all levels of government serve families, patients, and many others in today’s digital world.

The work we do matters.
## About the job
At Skylight, software engineers design, implement, and maintain software systems to improve government services for users. This software is built to meet the needs of regular users of government services as well as Skylight’s partners in government.
Skylight is partnering with a U.S. Air Force program office that runs a portfolio of civil engineering systems. These systems serve users across civil engineering, security forces, and services, including readiness managers, range personnel, and fire and emergency services. Releases are slow today. Regression testing is manual, security review happens after development finishes, and code freeze to production can take a month or more. We’ll move the program to an outcome-driven model with test automation and security built into the pipeline, starting with migrating the first application onto a DoD software factory. Leadership wants this office to become the model other Air Force offices adopt.
In this role, you’ll own test strategy across the portfolio and lead the move from manual to automated regression, so the team can ship with confidence and say clearly when a release is ready.
## What to know going in
Your first 30 days are about working with the Skylight team and government personnel, learning how the program office gets changes to users today, and understanding where testing and security slow things down. This is new work that replaces a traditional support model, so part of the job is coaching your government partners to keep these practices running after we leave. Expect to work alongside government engineers and other contractors, with tools and processes changing as the work gets underway.
This role is contingent on Skylight being awarded the underlying contract. If we’re not awarded the contract, we’ll let you know promptly and discuss whether there are other opportunities that fit.
## What you’ll do
• Design the test strategy for a portfolio of web applications, and decide pragmatically what to automate first
• Build automated regression suites and integrate them into the CI/CD pipeline
• Move the team from manual to automated regression testing, shrinking the time from code freeze to production
• Lead a shared pool of four test engineers starting in February, and help them grow
• Communicate release confidence clearly to non-technical stakeholders
• Pair with and coach government testers and engineers so automated testing sticks after we leave

• Experience leading testers or a test effort
• Experience working in a government or regulated environment with formal security authorization (ATO)
• Experience working on cross-functional teams (product, design, engineering, ops) in iterative delivery
• A track record of staying aligned and accountable on remote teams
• A mindset and work approach that aligns with our core values
## Nice-to-haves
• Experience with Selenium or behavior-driven test tools like Cucumber, and test case management in Zephyr Scale
• Experience integrating automated tests into CI/CD, ideally GitLab CI
• Experience testing COTS-based systems such as Esri or IBM TRIRIGA
• Experience using AI-assisted tools for test generation, paired with disciplined review
• Experience delivering technology in government, regulated industries, or other public-benefit settings

• Continuously monitor news related to emerging cloud security threats and further develop your domain expertise
• Continuously stay abreast and enabled on new Wiz features and functionality
• Drive Adoption, Business Value Realization, and Customer Satisfaction – Ensure your book of customers are delighted and seeing value from their Wiz purchase

• Overall
• 5-8+ years of experience in technical customer-facing roles, ideally supporting a cloud / cloud-security product
• For example: Technical Account Manager, Professional Services, Solutions Engineering, Technical Support, Customer Success Engineer, and Architect.

• Strong problem-solving skills, with the ability to troubleshoot complex technical issues and drive resolution across nebulous structures, both internal and external
• Ability and willingness to continuously learn emerging cloud/security technologies

• Proven track record of successfully managing a book of business with 5-10+ customers
• Proven track record of building and maintaining relationships with enterprise clients, driving customer outcomes, and exceeding performance targets
• Ability and willingness to continuously enable customers on the Wiz platform and assist them in solving problems, ranging from trivial to highly complex

## About the role
Wunderkind is hiring a Technical Solutions Consultant for the Delivery team in Existing Business. You'll be the post-sale technical expert for our live US and EMEA clients: diagnosing tracking and data issues, auditing performance, and scoping technical asks for the right team. CSMs own the client relationship and renewal; you own the technical answer.
You'll work alongside a second Technical Solutions Consultant and partner closely with CSMs, Implementation Managers, Professional Services Engineering and Product.
## What you'll do
• Investigate live issues such as conversion integrity, revenue drops and tracking gaps, and drive them to a root cause and fix.
• Debug the Wunderkind WebSDK within data layers, GTM, Adobe Launch and Shopify using browser dev tools.
• Reconcile GA4 and Wunderkind attribution, and run conversion and capture-rate analysis that CSMs can take into renewal conversations.
• Run end-to-end performance audits of client setups and deliver clear recommendations.
• Set up and validate data transfers (SFTP, cloud buckets, APIs), including suppression and subscriber feeds.
• Advise clients on consent and CMP setup, such as OneTrust, so identity and consent flow correctly into their system of record and Wunderkind tags fire properly.
• Scope technical asks and product prerequisites into clear specs for Professional Services Engineering.
• Decide whether an issue is a client fix, an engineering fix or a product request, and route it with the right context.
• Share feature requests and bugs with Product based on patterns you see across accounts.
• Build playbooks, documentation and AI-assisted tools that make common investigations faster.
• Develop and exhibit technical subject matter expertise for Wunderkind, including implementation, integrations, architecture, security, compliance, deliverability, and product roadmap, becoming the trusted advisor of our clients' technical stakeholders
## What you'll bring
• 3+ years in a post-sale technical role at a SaaS or martech company, such as technical account management, solutions engineering, support escalations or implementation.
• Hands-on web tracking debugging: browser dev tools, data layers, GTM, Adobe Launch and Shopify.
• Working knowledge of major ESPs (Klaviyo, Salesforce Marketing Cloud, Braze, Bloomreach, Sailthru) and how signals & API connections work within them.
• Comfort with SFTP, cloud buckets, REST APIs and JSON, plus file mapping and validation.
• Attribution and conversion analytics, including why GA4 and a vendor platform report different numbers.
• Strong client-facing writing. You can explain a root cause to a marketer and a fix to an engineer.
• The ability to manage many accounts at once and keep clients and internal teams updated.
## Nice to have
• Mobile SDK experience (iOS, Android).
• Privacy and CMP knowledge, such as OneTrust, GDPR and CCPA.
• Light SQL or scripting (Python, JavaScript).
• Experience building AI-assisted tools or workflows.
## What success looks like
• Live issues are diagnosed quickly, with a clear root cause and owner.
• CSMs go into renewals with credible technical answers and audit findings.
• Common investigations become repeatable through documentation and tooling.
The base salary range for this role is $115,000.00 to $140,000.00. Actual compensation packages are based on several factors that are unique to each specific candidate; including but not limited to skill set, depth of experience, applicable certifications, and geographic work location. This may vary depending on living location and market rate.

Start your adventure with Zip
Join Zip's Engineering team and put your name to solving fascinating quality challenges at scale in an agile, AI-forward development environment. If you bring a strong quality mindset, deep technical expertise, and a relentless curiosity to uncover edge cases and hidden defects, you'll be a great fit with the squads responsible for building cloud-native software applications that serve millions of customers and process billions of dollars in payments.

## Overview
Millennium is proud to be part of the Markon enterprise, a network of specialized organizations united in support of critical national security missions. This partnership strengthens our ability to deliver results by expanding our technical depth, operational reach, and access to a broader bench of proven experts, ensuring our customers continue to receive best-in-class cybersecurity support.Since 2004, Millennium has operated at the forefront of cybersecurity. Our elite team of over 300 professionals brings an unmatched record of performance across Red Team Operations, Defensive Cyber Operations, Software Engineering, and Technical Engineering. As home to the largest contingent of contracted Red Team operators supporting the Department of Defense, Millennium delivers unparalleled threat intelligence and battle-tested expertise to both DoD and federal civilian customers.
## What We Believe
Millennium is an equal opportunity employer and does not discriminate or allow discrimination on the basis of race, color, religion, gender, age, national origin, citizenship, disability, veteran status or any other classification protected by federal, state, or local law.
## Responsibilities
Millennium Corporation is hiring a Software Test Engineer to work 100% REMOTE . The candidate must have an active secret clearance.
Duties -
• Manages the planning, design, execution and reporting for software tests. May supervise junior testers.
• Provides administrative support by reviewing business / software requirements and provides inputs on requirement gaps, testability, and methodology.
• Provides administrative support by reviewing program documentation and products for quality and adherence to design concepts.
• Assists in preparing milestone status reports and deliveries/ presentations on the system concept to colleagues, end user representatives.
• Supports coordination of Cybersecurity T&E IAW DoDI 5000.02 and the DoD Risk Management Framework.
• Prepare / review test plans.
• Prepare test cases, test scripts and analyzes test data and ensures traceability to requirements.
• Works with the software development group throughout the development process.
• Supports the software configuration management process and understands all software components and their interface requirements.
• Performs software testing at all levels from module or unit testing through all levels of software integration testing and user acceptance tests (manual / automated).
• Reports defects and tracks defects and their status throughout the defect management process.
• Analyze test results and track software testing metrics.
• Supports the test lead with the creation of test reports.
• Train, mentor and supervise junior software engineers.
## Qualifications
• Candidate must have an active secret clearance.
• BS & 8 yrs of experience or HS Diploma and 13 yrs of experience.
• Required -Security+ certification. AWS Cloud practitioner cert preferred.
## Business Development
Assist with Business Development activities as required to support Millennium's strategic business objectives, which may include but not limited to participation in technical interviews, creation of technical documentation, general proposal writing support and proposal color reviews.
## Physical Requirements
• Must be comfortable with prolonged periods of sitting at a desk and working on a computer.
• Must be able to lift up to 10-15 pounds at a time.
## Travel Requirements
<10%
## COMPENSATION:
$115,000-$120,000
The salary range provided for this position is intended as a general guideline and does not guarantee a specific salary or compensation amount. Final compensation will be determined based on a variety of factors, including, relevant education, experience, knowledge, skills, and abilities.

### **The Role**
SDVI’s SDETs set the test strategy for the projects they support. You’ll work with feature developers to agree on what needs to be true for us to ship with confidence, then design, build, and run the test infrastructure that proves it. The work centers on how Rally behaves as a system, under load, under failure, and in the ways customers use it, more than on how any one part is implemented. We don’t measure SDET by how many defects it finds. We measure whether the risk we accept at release is risk we chose.
As a Senior SDET, you’ll drive test strategy for a major project or area of Rally with minimal direction. You’ll shape the test infrastructure the rest of the team builds on, and help other SDETs and feature developers raise the quality of their tests.
### **What You’ll Work On**
• Implement test strategy with feature teams on a major project or area of Rally, and agree up front on what must be true for high-impact changes and who proves it
• Test Rally against defined system properties and invariants, especially those pertaining to scalability, resiliency, and performance at customer scale
• Design test infrastructure and fixtures that serve both test and development, weigh their tradeoffs with peers, and see them through implementation to adoption
• Build tests that return a clear verdict on well-defined system behaviors
• Advise feature developers as they own the development-loop tests for their own changes
• Test that Rally’s failures are diagnosable, so customers and support can tell what broke and why
• Review past production incidents with Support Engineering to find gaps in how we test
• Mentor other SDETs, and improve the practices and tools the team uses
### **What Success Looks Like**
• **First 90 days.** You’re shaping the test strategy for a major project, know the test infrastructure well enough to support and refine its design, and feature teams coordinate with you to ensure releases ship with confidence.
• **First year.** You drive test strategy for a major area of Rally and have defined and tested its system properties. Feature developers use fixtures you designed, and other SDETs come to you for guidance.
### **What You’ll Bring**
• A track record of driving test strategy for microservice-based systems, cloud-hosted systems, or single-page web applications with minimal direction
• Experience designing test infrastructure and frameworks, and explaining their tradeoffs to peers
• Experience testing how systems behave under load and failure, beyond functional correctness
• Experience applying AI agents to test work, or driving test on an AI-forward engineering team, and a clear sense of when agent-written tests check the implementation instead of the intent
• Strong ability to read and understand Python, Javascript, or another programming language commonly used in test
• Experience applying software or system design principles in the test domain
• Curiosity about how and why systems fail, and the discipline to learn new systems and technologies in depth
• The ability to explain deeply technical topics to non-technical audiences, and to adjust how you communicate for customers, management, or peers
### **Nice to Have**
• Experience with load, performance, or fault-injection testing tools
• Experience running automated tests in CI pipelines
• Experience with pytest or similar test frameworks

• Experience mentoring other engineers
• Familiarity with professional media formats and tools, such as codecs, container formats, media encoders, and metadata management
If you don’t meet every point above, we’d still like to hear from you.
### **How We Work**
• **We’re small and distributed.** Most of our collaboration happens over Slack and Zoom, across time zones. You’ll own what you build, and you’ll work closely with people outside your immediate team.
• **Engineers stay close to customers.** You’ll hear directly from the people using what you build. When something goes wrong in production, the team that owns the code helps fix it.
• **We dig for root causes.** When something breaks, we find out why instead of patching the symptom and moving on.
• **We ship, then refine.** We work in short sprints and improve things over time instead of waiting for a perfect first version.
### **How We Use AI**
AI coding agents are part of how we work every day, and we invest in getting good at using them. We’re also careful with them, because customers run their content operations on Rally. We’re tracking industry trends and innovations, but using our day-to-day experiences to separate signal from noise.
Our engineers are still responsible for the code they ship. We still expect them to explain and defend its architecture and intent, even as more is built with an agent’s help. We judge work by its quality, not its quantity.

Manual testing here is targeted exploratory discovery — the critical and edge cases, the accessibility gaps, the things automation won't catch — rather than high-volume regression.
Most importantly, you'll be an integral part of maturing the product engineering culture of BibleProject, setting and maintaining a high bar with regard to our standards and people, and working to create an environment where great technical professionals like yourself can ship work worthy of our mission at a sustainable pace that reflects the BibleProject values: creative, humble, thoughtful, unifying, generous, and unhurried.
Core Functions
Leadership
• Own the App squad's automation suite and quality roadmap independently — build, maintain, and evolve it without ongoing pairing support.
• Own test strategy across the pyramid: identify where tests are needed — unit, component, integration, end-to-end — and partner with engineers to close gaps, influencing scope and sequencing based on risk and user impact.
• Champion shift-left practices: drive testability in design reviews and codify quality engineering standards and patterns.
• Partner with Product, Design, DevOps, and Data to define testable acceptance criteria (usability, accessibility, offline/edge-case behavior) and align on SLOs and release readiness.
• Drive continuous improvement: identify bottlenecks in CI/CD, observability, and environments, and deliver measurable fixes.
Responsibilities
• Build and maintain the automation suite with durable patterns, stable test data, and reliable test environments across iOS and Android.
• Track coverage gaps as the product evolves, and partner with engineers to get unit and component-level tests written and maintained in the codebase.
• Integrate tests into CI/CD with clear gates, fast feedback, and actionable reporting, driving down flaky failures over time.
• Plan and execute targeted exploratory testing on critical flows, new designs, and edge cases — offline/poor-connectivity behavior, accessibility gaps, and other issues automation won't catch — documenting reproducible steps and user impact.
• Establish, track, and improve quality signals (defect rate, change-failure rate, test stability, coverage depth, crash-free rate); validate releases using production signals and lead post-release verification for high-risk launches.
Expertise
• Mobile test automation: hands-on building and maintaining mobile UI automation suites from durable, maintainable patterns rather than one-offs; experience with Appium and the Page Object Model is a plus.
• Observability and analysis: using logs, metrics, traces, and crash reporting to validate behavior and identify defects quickly.
• Mobile quality judgment: offline and poor-connectivity correctness, behavior across a wide device range, mobile performance budgets and their user impact, and the release constraints of shipping through app stores.
• Product fluency for mobile: fluent in iOS and Android conventions, able to identify and articulate why something that technically passes still violates expected user experience.
• UX, accessibility, and AI-assisted quality: practical accessibility techniques for mobile and qualitative usability methods, plus comfort using AI-assisted tools to generate test ideas and data, summarize signals, and draft reports with human review and privacy-safe handling.
What We're Looking For
• 5+ years of experience (or equivalent skill) building and maintaining automated tests and quality tooling in a product team, including production software at scale.
• Demonstrated ability to build and own a mobile automation suite independently — designing stable tests, integrating them into a delivery pipeline, and driving down flakiness — without ongoing pairing support.
• Track record of risk-based coverage analysis: identifying where tests add the most value across a product and partnering with engineers to close gaps.
• Proven experience using production signals and observability to guide testing strategy and risk mitigation.
• Demonstrated ability to translate usability, accessibility, and performance expectations into testable acceptance criteria.
• Track record of surfacing blockers early and driving them to resolution without recurring escalation.
• Track record of giving and incorporating feedback, with demonstrated growth in scope of ownership over time.
• Alignment with BibleProject's mission and values.
About BibleProject
Portland, Oregon, Founded in 2014
BibleProject is an educational technology and media studio whose mission is to help people experience the Bible as a unified story that leads to Jesus.
We have grown significantly in the area of multimedia technology. What began with two animated videos now encompasses multiple platforms and products—including over 200 videos. Our website and app serve as connection hubs to our ever-growing library of resources. Classroom, our online learning platform, offers accessible, graduate-level Bible classes.
These, and all of our supporting products, continue to be completely free to audiences around the world, thanks to the ongoing generosity of our patrons.
Location: This role can be performed from anywhere in the United States. Occasional travel to Portland, OR, may be required.
Beginning: November 2026
Reporting to: Jeffrey Pearce, Group Engineering Manager, Audience Experience

• Competitive salary that scales with experience directly related to this role. Top tier in the non-profit market but will not match top technology companies.

We discuss and design architectures, review code, and research new front-end technologies. We talk to our clients directly, guiding them through the process, identifying potential problems and unknowns, and tackling challenges.
We help one another freely. We keep a Slack channel called ask-help, which is constantly used. We develop new skills, build better developer tools, and work on new types of projects regularly—and we take the time to present at conferences, give training, and run meetups. We’re huge devotees of open source, and our developer community is second to none.
Our fully remote team comprises about 70 developers and designers in the US and Canada. We welcome diversity and non-traditional paths into professions - we want the right person , not the right collection of tech keywords.
You can learn more about us with this short read: Hello Potential Bitovian .

Consult and Manage. You’ll consult and meet with clients regularly to learn about their needs and update them on the progress of their projects . You’ll provide product and/or delivery process leadership and work collaboratively with stakeholders and the technical delivery team. The bulk of your day will be spent on the following:
• Actively participating in roadmap planning and help align product initiatives with business objectives and strategies
• Implementing Bitovi’s approach to Agile program management to produce accurate, actionable plans at scale. You can read more about our methodology on the Agile Program Management training page in the Bitovi Academy .
• Delivering business and technical expertise to the feature teams for the purpose of completing the design, coding, testing, and implementation phases of the project life cycle
• Developing technical requirements from business requirements and prioritize them. Break requirements down to workable sizes and user stories
• Managing and appropriately escalating risks, issues, and changes
• Managing and refining the product backlog, assembling sprints, and performing release planning
• Participating in the release process as the product expert to surface any issues prior to the release
• Ensuring that roadmaps and the product backlog are visible, transparent, and clear to brand partners
Travel. Travel averages 3-5 days every quarter, and we’ll always be working with your schedule.
Teach. With Bitovi’s full support, you’ll have protected time to present at conferences, give training, plan and run meetups or local groups, and create various kinds of content in your area of expertise.

First and foremost, you’ll be part of a thoughtful, talented, and amazing team that supports and challenges one another to do their most exceptional work. • Completely remote work with flexible hours

Please follow application directions!

The QA Lead is accountable for the quality assurance practice across product delivery, ensuring that software is testable, test execution is timely and transparent, critical defects are surfaced early, and releases meet agreed quality standards. This role leads day-to-day QA planning and execution, strengthens automation and regression coverage, coaches QA team members, and works closely with Product Owners and Engineering to embed quality throughout the software development lifecycle rather than treating testing as a final-stage activity.
The QA Lead is expected to create clear visibility into test readiness, progress, risk, and blockers. The role owns the operating discipline of QA: defining test approaches, ensuring execution begins when planned, maintaining useful quality metrics, driving defect triage, and escalating issues early when delivery or release quality is at risk.
Key Responsibilities
Quality Leadership & Accountability
• Own the day-to-day QA practice and establish consistent expectations for test planning, execution, documentation, and release readiness.
• Ensure QA work begins when planned and that delays, blockers, environment issues, data needs, or scope gaps are identified and communicated immediately.
• Create transparency into what has been tested, what remains untested, current defects, quality risks, and confidence in release readiness.
• Hold QA team members accountable for execution commitments, timely updates, accurate status reporting, and follow-through.
• Coach QA team members on testing discipline, risk-based thinking, root-cause analysis, and stronger ownership of outcomes.
Test Strategy, Planning & Execution
• Develop and maintain test strategies for new features, enhancements, integrations, defects, and platform changes.
• Partner with Product Owners early in discovery and refinement to identify test scenarios, edge cases, data needs, dependencies, and acceptance criteria before development is complete.
• Ensure test cases provide adequate functional, integration, regression, negative, end-to-end, and workflow coverage based on business and technical risk.

• Use AI coding agents and related tools to explore the SDK codebases, understand behaviour and accelerate quality work.

What Good Looks Like
You will be succeeding when:
• Important SDK behaviours have dependable automated protection;
• Useful quality improvements land incrementally and are easy for the team to adopt;
• SDK-to-platform integration failures are detected early and are easy to diagnose;
• Tests run reliably in the workflows the team actually uses;
• Test failures give the team enough information to act;
• Well-understood defects are followed through to an appropriate fix or clear handover;
• Repeated quality problems become better tests, tooling or product changes;
• Automation and risk-based exploration provide evidence proportionate to the change;
• Your communication makes quality risks and next actions easy to understand;

As a Senior QA Engineer at Watu, you are embedded in a squad - the senior technical authority on quality within it. You do everything a QA Engineer does - ceremonies, acceptance criteria, automated test suites, the Definition of Done - but you also own the harder problems: test architecture, performance and load testing, contract testing, and the squad's most complex integration surfaces.
You report to your squad's Tech Lead for day-to-day work. For QA standards and tooling, you sit in the QA Chapter led by the QA Chapter Lead, who reports to the Head of Engineering. You are the natural deputy to the QA Chapter Lead - representing your squad in the QA Guild when needed, mentoring QA Engineers across the chapter, and often owning a specific chapter-wide initiative (a framework, a tooling migration, a testing discipline) end to end.

• Own test architecture for your squad's domain - the structure of the test pyramid, how unit, integration, contract, and E2E tests fit together, and where the squad's coverage gaps are.
• Lead performance and load testing for your squad - establishing baselines, identifying throughput and concurrency limits, and surfacing risk before it reaches production.
• Own the squad's Definition of Done quality gate, and act as the final internal check before anything ships to staging or production.
• Mentor QA Engineers in your squad and across the chapter - reviewing their test design, raising the bar on automation quality, and helping them grow into the standards the Chapter Lead sets.
• Deputise for the QA Chapter Lead where needed - representing your squad's QA practice in the monthly QA Guild, and contributing directly to chapter-wide standards, tooling decisions, and onboarding material.
• Own a chapter-level initiative - for example, the contract-testing framework, the performance-testing toolkit, or AI-assisted test generation - evaluating, implementing, and documenting it for the whole function.
• Triage the squad's hardest test failures - distinguishing flaky tests from real regressions in complex, high-traffic, or high-risk areas of the system.
• Use AI/LLM tooling actively: test case generation, synthetic test data, regression triage, and documentation are all areas where AI accelerates QA work.
## Who You Are
## Essential
• 5+ years of QA engineering experience in a software product environment, with a track record of owning test strategy for a complex domain, not just executing within it.
• Strong automation engineering skills - you write test code to a production standard, in Java, Python, or JavaScript, and your suites are maintainable, readable, and stable in CI.

We're revolutionizing how data centers operate across North America, Western Europe, and Israel, serving the world's leading technology and hyperscale companies. With Manulife Investment Management's acquisition in 2023 and our award-winning InCommand platform we're positioned for explosive growth as AI adoption and cloud migration drive unprecedented demand for data center capacity.

It will be delivered as a cloud service and be deployable in customers' own environments, built API-first, and developed with an agent-assisted engineering practice in which coding agents work from specifications under human review. Our own facilities are the first customer, so everything we build is proven in real, live operations before anyone else sees it.
Everything the product shows an operator starts at the site: the power chain, the cooling plant, the IT equipment, the building systems, each speaking its own protocol. Getting that data in reliably, from the first facility to the hundredth, is a discipline of its own, and as Integration Lead you own it. It is a clean-sheet design with a rare advantage: a real estate of live data centers to learn from and the people who have kept their data flowing for a decade sitting beside you. You partner closely with Architecture, Product Management and Developer Platform, and you lead and manage a small integrations team that grows as the sites multiply.
## Key Accountabilities
Design and own the edge collector: store-and-forward, buffering, configuration and upgrades across a fleet of sites, secure outbound-only connectivity across OT and IT network boundaries.
Define, in partnership with Architecture, the contract by which site data enters the platform, and own the collector side of it.
Build or select the protocol adapters for building automation, power and cooling systems, IT equipment and monitoring gateways, each with a conformance test.
Own point mapping and normalisation into the unified asset, power and cooling model: templates, discovery, bulk mapping and validation of a site's data before it goes live.
Automate site onboarding so that bringing a new site live takes days rather than weeks, and measure it by the time it takes to onboard the next one.
Make telemetry health visible and owned: data flow, gaps and staleness, with the alerts to match.
Assess the telemetry stack in use today and recommend its future.

8+ years in software or controls engineering, including 3+ leading integrations for industrial IoT, building automation, DCIM or similar operational-technology products.
You have integrated equipment over the protocols a data center speaks (BACnet/IP, Modbus TCP and RTU, SNMP, OPC UA, Redfish or IPMI, MQTT), reading vendors' register maps and making them work.
You have designed and shipped collector or agent software running at the edge across a fleet of sites, with store-and-forward, remote configuration and upgrades, and secure outbound-only connectivity (TLS, mutual TLS, certificate management).
You have built point mapping and normalisation at scale, with discovery, templates and validation, and made each site faster to onboard than the last.
You have delivered site data into a platform through MQTT brokers (EMQX, HiveMQ or equivalent) and Kafka-compatible streaming (Kafka, Redpanda or equivalent), landing in time-series storage (TimescaleDB, InfluxDB or equivalent).
You have packaged and operated edge software in containers (Docker, k3s or equivalent) with fleet or device management across many sites.
You have written adapters, mapping tooling and automation in Python.
You have built monitoring of telemetry health (data flow, gaps, staleness) with OpenTelemetry, Grafana or equivalent.

Built on industrial edge or SCADA platforms (Ignition, Node-RED, Telegraf or equivalent) and decided when to build and when to buy at the edge.
Modelled building and equipment data with Project Haystack or Brick Schema, or used MQTT Sparkplug B.
Applied operational-technology security standards (IEC 62443 or equivalent) and OT/IT network segmentation.
Worked with data-center electrical and mechanical systems (switchgear, UPS, PDUs and busways, chillers and CRAHs, liquid cooling) and the data they produce.
Led the evaluation and migration of a telemetry or monitoring platform.
Led or managed a small team of engineers.

## About Supermove
Supermove builds software and AI for moving companies. We've raised $30M from Andreessen Horowitz (a16z) and other investors. We started in 2019 as the system that runs a moving business: sales, operations, crews, billing. Today that system runs moving companies across the US, Canada and Australia, from single-location movers to some of the largest van lines and franchise systems in North America.
Now we're putting AI to work on top of it. Our voice agents answer and call leads, book moves, and hand off to a person at the right moment. Autopilot, our agent platform, goes further. It answers questions about the business in plain language, flags what needs attention, and handles work that used to take a person's whole day, from working the inbox to updating jobs.
## The role
Every moving company runs on its own logic: its own rates and tariffs, its own way of paying crews and commissioning salespeople, its own accounting system, and often a van line with rules of its own. When a customer signs, someone has to turn all of that into a working Supermove account. That's you.
You'll own implementations from kickoff to go-live and a clean handoff to our customer success team, running several at once. On our largest accounts, you'll work alongside a Key Account Director who owns the relationship and the results. You own the build.
This is a hands-on role. You won't write requirements and hand them to someone else. You'll be inside Supermove every day, configuring, testing, and tracing why an invoice or a sync came out wrong. The people who love this job would rather be in the tool than reporting on it.
## What you'll do
Run implementations from kickoff to go-live: discovery, configuration, testing, training, launch. Set the dates and hold the customer and our team to them.
Turn how a customer charges and pays into working configuration: pricing and tariffs, billing formulas, hourly minimums, crew pay, and salesperson and contract-driver commissions.
Design account structures for multi-location companies and franchise systems, and build master templates that dozens or hundreds of locations can start from.
Set up and fix accounting integrations. Map the general ledger, get invoices and vendor bills flowing to Sage Intacct or QuickBooks, and help the customer's finance team reconcile.
Connect customers to their van lines (Unigroup, SIRVA and others) so orders, statements and settlements flow without retyping.
Set up voice agents and Autopilot workflows with the customer. Decide where the AI acts on its own and where a person signs off, then listen to real calls and fix what's failing.
Use AI agents to do the work faster: investigating issues, drafting configuration, working through data, answering customer questions. Then help define what our own configuration and Autopilot agents should do next.
Turn what customers run into into clear bug reports and product requests, with screenshots and the customer's own words, and follow them through with engineering.
Train customer teams, from office staff to crews, around how they'll actually use the system, not a generic tour of features.
Improve how we implement. Own the templates, checklists, QA and handoff steps, and teach new team members.
## What this role asks of you
Comfort with how money moves. You know what a general ledger, AP and AR, a vendor bill and a reconciliation are, and you can talk to a controller in their language.
Logic and formulas. You can turn a commission sheet or a rate contract into rules a system can run, and spot the case that breaks them.
Comfort ahead of the documentation. We're putting AI into an industry that's never had it, so there's often no runbook yet. You'll design the approach while running it, then write it down so the next implementation starts further ahead.
AI as a working tool. You already use AI to get more done, not as a novelty. Candidates who've built it into how they work stand out.
Patience with a low-tech user base. Dispatchers, sales reps, and owners who've run the same way for twenty years. Changing how they work takes credibility on the ground as much as a project plan.
## What we're looking for
5+ years implementing or configuring complex business software (ERP, accounting, payroll, field-service, or vertical SaaS) for customers, owning the go-live. Experience with field-heavy businesses like construction, home services, fleet or logistics is a plus.
Accounting or bookkeeping experience is a big plus.
Technical enough to troubleshoot. You understand APIs, webhooks and data syncs well enough to tell where something broke. SQL or light scripting is a plus.
You've run several projects at once without dropping any, and you can tell us how.
Clear and steady with customers, whether you're training a dispatcher or telling a controller why the numbers don't match yet.
You write clearly. A lot of this job happens in writing.
Moving, van-line or relocation experience is a plus. We'll teach you the industry.
## Why this role matters
A moving company trusts us with how it quotes, bills, pays its people and closes its books. If implementation gets that right, everything built on top of it works, AI included. You'll shape how we implement as we grow into larger and more complex customers, and how our own AI agents take on more of this work.

## About Supermove
Supermove builds software and AI for moving companies. We've raised $30M from Andreessen Horowitz (a16z) and other investors. We started in 2019 as the system that runs a moving business: sales, operations, crews, billing. Today that system runs moving companies across the US, Canada and Australia, from single-location movers to some of the largest van lines and franchise systems in North America.
Now we're putting AI to work on top of it. Our voice agents answer and call leads, book moves, and hand off to a person at the right moment. Autopilot, our agent platform, goes further. It answers questions about the business in plain language, flags what needs attention, and handles work that used to take a person's whole day, from working the inbox to updating jobs.
## The role
We're hiring a Founding Forward Deployed Engineer to help build and lead our Forward Deployed Engineering function alongside Supermove's founders.
Our largest customers operate hundreds of locations, with thousands of employees, complex workflows, and multiple systems that need to work together. Getting AI to work reliably inside these businesses is a hard engineering problem. That's where you come in.
You'll work directly with our largest customers to understand how their businesses operate, build and deploy AI solutions, and make sure they deliver real results. This isn't a role where you hand requirements to engineering and wait for someone else to build them. You'll write production code, improve our AI agents, build integrations, and solve technical problems yourself.
You'll also work closely with our product and engineering teams to turn what you learn in the field into improvements to the core platform. The goal isn't to build a different solution for every customer. It's to figure out what works, make it reusable, and help us scale it.
As one of our first Forward Deployed Engineers, you'll work directly alongside the founders to define how this function operates, from the technical tools and deployment processes to how we hire and develop the team over time.
## What you'll do
Build and lead the FDE function. Work alongside the founders to establish the engineering practices, tooling, and processes for deploying AI at enterprise scale. Help shape and grow the team as we expand.
Ship production code. Build and improve AI agents, integrations, and core product capabilities. Work directly in our codebase to solve customer problems and improve the platform.
Lead technical deployments for major accounts. Own the technical execution from discovery and solution design through implementation, testing, go-live, and ongoing improvement. Work across engineering, product, and customer teams to get things done.
Design AI solutions for real operations. Understand how a customer works and determine how our Voice Agents and Autopilot should fit into their business, including where AI can take action and where people need to stay involved.
Make AI agents work reliably. Review calls and agent sessions, investigate failures, improve prompts and workflows, fix underlying code, and measure performance in production.
Turn customer problems into product improvements. Identify patterns across deployments and build reusable capabilities rather than one-off solutions. Help shape the technical roadmap based on what customers actually need.
Deliver measurable results. Make sure what you build works in production and creates real value for customers. Use data to understand performance, identify problems, and demonstrate impact.
## What we're looking for
4+ years of software engineering experience, with a track record of building and shipping production systems.
Strong full-stack or backend engineering skills. You're comfortable working across APIs, databases, integrations, and complex application logic.
Experience building with LLMs, AI agents, or AI-powered workflows. You understand the challenges of making probabilistic systems work reliably in production.
You've owned technically complex projects end to end, from understanding the problem and designing a solution to writing code, deploying it, and making sure it works.
You're comfortable working directly with customers. You can explain technical tradeoffs to a CEO or COO and work with frontline operators to understand how their business actually runs.
You can lead without needing a large team or formal authority. You're comfortable coordinating engineers and other stakeholders, making decisions, and driving work forward.
You thrive in ambiguity. You don't need a perfectly defined spec to get started, and you're willing to dig into unfamiliar systems to figure out how things work.
You use AI seriously in your own work and are constantly experimenting with new tools and approaches to build faster and better.
Moving, logistics, or field-services experience is a plus. We'll teach you the industry.
## Why this role matters
We're at the beginning of bringing AI into some of the largest moving companies in North America. These businesses have complicated operations, and making AI work inside them requires more than building a good model or a polished demo.
You'll be one of the first engineers responsible for bridging that gap. You'll work directly with customers, build production AI systems, and help determine how we turn successful deployments into a scalable product.
You'll also work alongside Supermove's founders to build a new engineering function from the ground up, with significant influence over its technical direction, how it operates, and the team we build around it.
You'll have the opportunity to build the product, lead real-world deployments, and help shape the engineering team that brings AI into an entire industry.
## Process
Intro call → technical interview → practical engineering exercise → founder interview.

Twingate is building a modern remote access solution that simplifies and improves the way businesses secure access to their cloud, SaaS, and on-prem resources. Twingate is backed by leading investors such as BOND, WndrCo, 8VC, Green Bay Ventures, SignalFire, and Dropbox founders Drew Houston and Arash Ferdowsi. Our investors share our belief that in a world where workforces are becoming increasingly distributed, it is critical to be able to effectively secure access to apps, data, and environments.
As part of our company culture, our belief in putting the customer first permeates our thinking in everything from our customer communications to the design process behind the product itself. If you take pride in creating experiences with the customer firmly at the center of the picture, we'd love to work with you.
## About Twingate
For thirty years, securing access to a company's systems has meant making them harder to use. The VPN is the clearest example: a tunnel into the whole network, slow for the people who need it and trusted far more than it deserves. The industry's answer has been more layers and more acronyms. We think that is the wrong direction.
Twingate exists to prove that the most secure way to do something can also be the easiest. A user opens their laptop and the application is simply there. Behind that, every connection is checked against who the person is, what device they are on, and what they are allowed to reach, and nothing else is visible. Security people do not have to think about is the only kind that actually gets used.
We sell to IT and security teams, and increasingly to engineers: some companies embed Twingate inside their own products and platforms. From startups to large enterprises, the deal is won or lost on whether the product does what we say in the customer's real environment. That is where Solutions Engineering lives. Our customers say it better than we do: twingate.com/customers.
## The role
Most solutions engineers are measured on whether the demo went well. You will be measured on whether the technical evaluation produced a decision, and on making that decision a success for the customer.
You own the technical journey for our largest and most complex opportunities, from discovery through technical close and into production. Your job is to make sure the customer ends up with what they actually need, which is rarely what they first asked for, and that the people who championed Twingate internally are proven right for having done so.
Everyone on our team takes it personally when a customer does not get real value from what we build. We want someone who shares that mindset: the kind of person who opens doors for others without expecting a thank you, and who keeps asking what a customer experience could look like if nobody had done it that way before. Our shorthand for it: good service is giving champagne when asked. Great service is giving champagne at the right moment, before being asked.
## Responsibilities
Run technical evaluations that end in a decision. You and the customer agree in writing, before the work starts, on what success looks like and which requirements are deal-breakers. You keep that agreement current, call it early when a deal-breaker cannot be met, and separate what the evidence shows from what you were told.
Qualify properly, including out. Before you propose anything, you know why the customer should do anything at all, why now, and who cares. You turn vague terms into testable behavior, pull on every thread of a multi-part answer instead of acknowledging it and moving on, and find the driver behind the request rather than the solution the customer proposed. People are good at normalizing pain; you do not take "we don't have much" at face value. When we are not the right fit, you say so early.
Find and build technical champions. Behind every Twingate deployment is someone who put their credibility on the line to bring us in. Your job is to make that person successful: anticipate what they will need before they ask, give them what they need to make the case internally, and make sure the win is theirs. You give more than you get, every time.
Go deep when it is needed, and know when it is not. You can go as deep as any engineer in the room needs, and you can explain the same idea to someone who has never opened a terminal. The skill is reading the composition of the audience and adjusting automatically, so that nobody is left behind and nobody is bored. You are the customer's primary educator, and you are intentional about delivering value to every person on the call regardless of their technical background.
Leave the team better than you found it. Your trackers, guides, demo environments, and product feedback are built so others can use them without you in the room. You give teammates direct feedback on their qualification. And the relationship does not end at the signature: you stay directly involved through onboarding once a prospect becomes a customer, because the person who ran the evaluation is the person who knows what was promised. Continuity matters to us.
## Qualifications
• 8+ years in a customer-facing technical role, including several on enterprise deals with multiple technical stakeholders.
• Technical evaluations you scoped and ran yourself that ended in a clear win or a clear, early disqualification.
• Practical networking knowledge: how TCP and UDP connections are established, how DNS resolves, how TLS authenticates two parties, what NAT does to a packet, and ideally how to read a packet capture.
• Hands-on with at least one major cloud, Kubernetes, and an identity provider such as Okta, Entra ID, or Google Workspace. Endpoint security and device management tools (CrowdStrike, Intune, Jamf) are a strong plus.
• Scripting in Python, Bash, or PowerShell, and working with REST and GraphQL APIs. Enough to automate a test or build a small integration, not to ship software.
• A structured qualification method (MEDDPICC or similar). We care less which one and more whether you can show us yours from a real deal.
• Clear, succinct writing. Most of the value in this role is written.
• Familiarity with zero trust network access and adjacent categories helps but is not required. We can teach the market; we cannot teach intellectual curiosity.
## How You Work
These traits predict success in this role better than anything on the list above.
Driven by customer value. You measure yourself by whether the customer is better off, not by whether the deal closed. You go out of your way for people who may never know you did; you welcome credit but do not particularly thrive on it.
Resilient. Deals stall, champions leave, evaluations fail for reasons outside your control. You rebound on your own and are comfortable being uncomfortable.
Emotionally intelligent. You read a room from what people do, not only what they say: the stakeholder who has checked out, the champion under pressure, the "yes" that is a polite no.
Coachable

Application modernization and migration

## Description
SAIC is seeking a Senior Software Development Engineer in Test (SDET) to join the Joint Range Extension (JRE) software development team.
This is a REMOTE ROLE within the UNITED STATES. MUST BE A U.S. CITIZEN. This role will involve up to 10% of CONUS travel.
JRE is a combat-proven data link gateway that plays a vital role in the defense of the United States and our allies by extending the reach of tactical data across the battlespace and around the globe. It is a large, mission-critical, near-real-time system written predominantly in Java and Kotlin, and also includes C++ components. JRE is deployed everywhere from handheld devices and small-form-factor drones to strategic bombers, guided-missile destroyers, and global command-and-control centers.
As a Senior Software Development Engineer in Test (SDET) on the software development team, you'll work closely with other developers, as well as with testers and test engineers on the test team. Through test automation, you'll play an essential role in enabling rapid, agentically-developed, high-quality releases of JRE to meet the current and future mission needs of the warfighter.
Your impact will extend beyond the code you write yourself. You'll lead projects and build up the test engineering skills of the people you work with.
JOB DUTIES:
• Expand JRE's unit, integration, service, GUI, and end-to-end test automation .
• Engineer and maintain a comprehensive automated performance test suite covering load, stress, and endurance testing; support our IT team with capacity planning for the hardware environment it requires.
• Design, develop, and maintain advanced simulators for IP and serial tactical data link terminals, radios, navigation systems, and sensors.
• Contribute to the definition and ongoing verification of minimum system requirements for JRE's full range of deployment platforms.
• Refactor JRE code for testability, introducing API, RPC, and messaging seams to enable additional white- and gray-box testing.
• Mentor developers, testers, and less-experienced test engineers in test automation best practices as we expand automated coverage across the codebase.
• Optimize the performance and quality of our test automation suites.
• Quarantine, troubleshoot, and fix nondeterministic tests.
## Qualifications
Required Education:
• Bachelor's degree and nine (9) years’ experience; additional four (4) years’ experience can be considered in lieu of degree.
Required Clearance:
• Must have the ability to obtain and maintain an active Secret security clearance; US Citizenship required.
Required Skills:
• Deep expertise in the JVM and Java , with familiarity with Kotlin and Scala; strong concurrent programming skills (Threads, Executor Framework, Futures/Promises, Virtual Threads, Reactor, Kotlin Coroutines) and experience testing concurrent/asynchronous code (Reactor Test, Kotlinx Coroutines Test).
• Proven experience developing and maintaining high test automation coverage for large-scale (1M+ LOC), mission-critical, high-reliability, near-real-time systems, using JVM testing and mocking frameworks such as JUnit, AssertJ, Mockito, and MockK.
• Experience with automated performance testing and analysis using tools such as JMeter and Gatling, and with continuous integration and modern deployment practices for edge and cloud systems in Gradle-built projects.
• Familiarity with C++ and related test automation frameworks (Doctest, Google Mock), along with experience in network programming, networking protocols, low-level binary data processing, and distributed systems using RPC and message-oriented architectures.
• Thorough knowledge of object-oriented and functional design patterns; software design principles; refactoring techniques; code and test smells; domain-driven design; and a proven track record leading successful large-scale, phased refactoring initiatives.
• Experience mentoring developers and testers in test automation best practices; strong skills with dependency injection and the Spring ecosystem (Spring Boot, Spring Data, Spring Security) and their integration testing utilities; and a collaborative, test-driven, iterative development style using Agile methods (Scrum, Extreme Programming, Lean) including pairing and mobbing.
Desired Skills:
• Public contributions to open-source projects.
• Familiarity with any of the following:
• Tactical data link standards such as MIL-STD-6016, MIL-STD-6017, MIL-STD-3011, MIL-STD-6020, MIL-STD-6040, MIL-STD-2525, MIL-STD-1553, etc.
• Tactical terminals and radios such as MIDS JTRS, STT, BATS-D, AN/ARC, and AN/PRC.
• Navigation and avionics standards such as NMEA 0183, GPS-153, ARINC 429, and ARINC 661.
• Security standards such as DISA STIGs, NIST SP 800-171, and NIST SP 800-207.

## About Practifi (The Real Story)
Practifi is the only intelligent CRM company that meets wealth management firms wherever they are in their AI adoption journey. Our enterprise-grade, compliance-first foundation brings client data, workflows, and relationship intelligence together in one system, so firms can understand what matters, take the right action, and scale without ever needing a new CRM.
That same directness runs through how we work. We're a team of fewer than 100 people, remote-first across the US and Australia, and we'd rather tell you how this job actually works than polish it for the pitch. We don't sell a version of the role that doesn't exist.
## The Opportunity (What This Role Really Means)
When a wealth management firm moves onto Practifi, the first thing they judge us on is their data. If a household is missing a member, if a client shows up twice, or if a servicing team points to the wrong advisor, they notice on day one. So do their clients.
Right now, quality assurance on those data migrations is handled by whoever is delivering the engagement, on top of everything else on their plate. It works, but it means every client gets a slightly different process and nobody has a clear view of the issues that keep coming back.

The Core Work
• Validate every migration end to end. • Check the details that matter. Every record carries a valid External Id and Batch Id, nothing is owned by a default system user, every contact is tied to at least one relationship, and counts reconcile to source or have a clear explanation.
• Log, route, and retest. You'll capture screenshots of failed checks, log findings in Asana and JIRA, route fixes to engineering, and retest once they're corrected.
• Report clearly. After each Initial Load and Final Load, you'll give the Project Manager, Consultant, or Business Analyst the metrics they need, and you'll prepare the final QA sign-off report before go-live.
• Raise the flag early. When a data issue puts a go-live at risk, you'll escalate it to the Project Manager within 24 hours
• Build the standard. You'll own one QA checklist and issue-tracking format for every engagement, replacing the client-by-client workbooks in use today, and you'll track recurring issues across clients so we fix the process, not just the record.
The Reality Check
The Practifi data model has its own vocabulary, and it takes time to learn how it all fits together. You won't figure it out alone. You'll complete the same onboarding and training curriculum as every individual contributor here, including our PractifiU learning platform, and you'll have a Practibuddy mentor from day one.
You'll also be working alongside Consultants, Business and Data Analysts, Data Engineers, and Project Managers. Part of the job is raising problems in a way that keeps projects moving. And when QA volume is lighter, you'll flex into delivery support, so you'll see the whole implementation, not just your portion of it.
The Growth
This is a new role, which means you'll shape it. The checklist, the reporting format, and the process improvements you contribute each quarter become part of how Data Services operates.
You'll earn a Salesforce certification once you're here, with time and support built in, and an annual Learnbucks stipend for the courses and certifications you choose after that. IFS Copperleaf helps the world’s largest asset-intensive organizations — utilities, energy, water, transportation, and more — decide where to invest billions in capital to deliver the most value, using AI-powered decision analytics. As a Forward Deployed Engineer, you sit cross-functionally across the Sales, Product, R&D, and Implementation teams. For our most critical pursuits, you stand up our current product on the customer’s own data, fast, to prove value inside the deal. And when a customer needs something our product does not yet do, you use modern AI tools to rapidly prototype a near-production ready solution and put it in front of them. You turn “we can’t do that” into “here’s how,” and the strongest prototypes go on to shape our roadmap.
You own the technical outcome from discovery through production adoption. Your job is to win deals by delivering fast and with value in the current production environment, prototyping and articulating value from customer requirements, measuring and proving value across customer workflows, and continuously coordinating field-observed customer needs, ideas, roadmaps, and visions with the product and sales organizations. You are the shaper that understands customers’ needs, hypothesizes on value, co-creates the solution, and can test, measure, and validate the outcomes.

• Work alongside Solutions Consultants and Account Executives with our most innovative and strategic accounts as well as our most important net new opportunities.
• Own discovery, technical scoping, architecture, implementation, evaluation, productionization, adoption, and handoff for strategic customer solutions. Deploy and prove value.
• Prototype aggressively; productionize deliberately.
• For sales and product management validation, build the smallest safe prototype that tests the hypothesis inside the deal’s timeline. For production use, engineer for security, reliability, observability, maintainability, and integration with the customer’s architecture.

• Work with Product continuously as business value emerges and outcomes become known to evaluate business potential, broader market needs, competitive differentiation aspects, and functional/technical specifications.

• Influenced ACV on deals where an FDE engaged.
• Time to first working prototype on the customer’s own data.
• Graduation rate: the share of prototypes that reach production.
• Patterns and accelerators shipped, and how often they get reused on later engagements.
• Recurring gaps taken to Product, and what Product decided.

This role exists to help ServiceNow partners adopt and succeed with Engage Central by combining solution consulting, onboarding and adoption, and first-line support in a single point of contact.
In this role, you will be a key member of the Customer Excellence Group (CEG), reporting to the Engage Central Product Director and supporting the sales, onboarding, and adoption of Engage Central with ServiceNow partners. Engage Central is ServiceNow’s unified engagement platform that gives Expert Services and partner consultants a common, AI-native way to deliver accelerated implementations from discovery through go-live.
This is a new, hybrid role that blends three disciplines: solution consulting, customer success, and first-line (L1) support. You will position and demonstrate Engage Central to partners, guide them through onboarding to productive use, and serve as their first point of contact when issues arise. You will work closely with Partner Managers, Partner Sales, Solution Consulting, CEG delivery, and the Engage Central product team. You will help build the motion, scale it to business-as-usual, and feed partner insight directly into the product roadmap.
What you get to do in this role:
Partner Sales & Solution Consulting
• Serve as the product and technical expert for Engage Central in partner sales cycles, working with Partner Managers, Partner Sales, and Solution Consultants to craft the value proposition for each partner
• Lead discovery sessions to understand partner delivery practices, challenges, and goals, and map them to Engage Central capabilities
• Deliver tailored product demonstrations and proof-of-value sessions that show how Engage Central accelerates partner delivery
• Answer product feature, technical, security, and access questions from partners and ServiceNow colleagues
• Build and maintain reusable sales assets — demo scripts, pitch decks, FAQs, and objection handling — and share best practices across the team
• Track partner pipeline and adoption status, and report progress and forecast to the Engage Central Product Director
Partner Onboarding & Adoption
• Own onboarding for a portfolio of partners, from kickoff and access provisioning through the first engagement delivered on Engage Central
• Build a success plan with each partner that sets clear adoption milestones and business outcomes
• Deliver enablement and training for partner leaders and consultants, and maintain onboarding guides, playbooks, and knowledge articles
• Monitor usage and adoption, identify at-risk partners early, and run targeted plays to drive deeper, sustained usage
• Capture partner success stories and use cases that demonstrate measurable value
• Coordinate with CEG delivery, Partner Managers, and the product team to ensure a seamless transition from sales to onboarding to steady state
L1 Support & Issue Resolution
• Act as the first point of contact for partner questions and issues with Engage Central, including access, navigation, configuration, and how-to requests
• Triage, troubleshoot, and resolve L1 issues within agreed service levels; escalate complex issues to product and engineering with clear reproduction steps and business impact
• Track issues through resolution and keep partners informed along the way
• Assist in turning recurring issues into knowledge articles, FAQs, and self-service content that reduce future support volume
• Help define and improve the Engage Central support model, intake process, and service levels as the program scales
Product Feedback & Continuous Improvement
• Serve as the voice of the partner, synthesizing insight from sales, onboarding, and support into clear, prioritized input for the product roadmap
• Participate in pilots, release reviews, and user acceptance testing to validate new capabilities before broad partner rollout
• Report regularly to leadership on adoption trends, support themes, and partner sentiment
• Identify opportunities to improve product usability based on feedback from partner and customers
## Qualifications
To be successful in this role you have:
• Experience in leveraging or critically thinking about how to integrate AI into work processes, decision-making, or problem-solving. This may include using AI-powered tools, automating workflows, analyzing AI-driven insights, or exploring AI’s potential impact on the function or industry.
• Experience supporting a new product launch or early-stage go-to-market motion
• Familiarity with support operations, including knowledge management and service levels (ITIL a plus)
• Experience in professional services delivery or consulting environments
• Knowledge of the ServiceNow partner ecosystem and partner delivery models
Nice to have:
• ServiceNow SPM certifications
• Travel, as necessary less than 20%
• ServiceNow Certified System Administrator certification
• Comfort working independently in a new, fast-changing role and building processes from the ground up
• Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to translate technical concepts for business audiences
• Experience working collaboratively with partners, professional services, product management, and sales teams
• Strong troubleshooting and problem-solving skills, with comfort triaging issues and partnering with engineering to resolve them
• A track record of driving onboarding, adoption, and value realization across a portfolio of customers or partners
• Proven ability to run discovery and deliver compelling product demonstrations to technical and business audiences
• Proficiency with the ServiceNow platform or technical expertise with cloud software solutions
• 7+ years of related experience in solution consulting, pre-sales, customer success, or technical account management, ideally including customer or partner support
